The dollar credit slightly decreased by 0.3%, partially reflecting dollar weakness, while other foreign currency credits grew strongly by 15.5% during the same period, mainly reflecting an increase in renminbi credit. Overall, due to the short-term fluctuation in The Hong Kong dollar credit caused by new share offerings activities, the total credit of the securities firms increased significantly by 13.2% during the review period (Figure 4.6). It should be noted that due to fluctuations caused by monthly currency statistics or various short-term factors (such as seasonality and public offering-related funding demands, as well as business and investment activities), statistical figures should be interpreted with caution. With the increase in total reserves, interbank rates among Hong Kong banks remained at extremely low levels overall during the review period (Figure 4.8). Due to the recurring economic downturn caused by the novel coronavirus epidemic, coupled with the impact of the long-term low-interest-rate environment, the profitability of Hong Kong's retail banks further decreased in the second half of 2020, and asset quality also slightly declined. Nevertheless, based on its capital and liquidity situation, the Hong Kong banks sector remains stable. During the review period, to continue supporting the overall economy through the difficulties, the Monetary Authority decided to extend several relief measures. Looking ahead, although the introduction of vaccines may inspire optimism that the global pandemic will be controlled and economic activities can resume, the pace of economic recovery remains unclear. The aforementioned uncertainties and ongoing geopolitical tensions will be detrimental to commercial activities and continue to pose challenges to the Hong Kong banks sector. Especially as the pandemic weakens the repayment capacity of enterprises and households, the banking sector should closely monitor the impact of relevant downside risk factors on its asset quality. In the second half of 2020, the overall pre-tax operating profit of retail banks fell by 38.5% compared to the same period in 2019. Accordingly, the asset return rates fell to 0.62% in the second half of 2020, compared to 1.13% the same period in 2019 (Figure 5.1). The net interest margin of retail banks narrowed from 1.63% in the second half of 2019 to 1.01% in the same period of 2020 (Figure 5.2), causing a decrease in net interest income and exceeding the slight increase in non-interest income, leading to a decline in profitability. For the full year 2020, the overall pre-tax operating profit of retail banks declined by 29.4%, and the return on assets fell from 1.19% in 2019 to 0.77%. Figure 5.1 Profitability of Retail Banks Figure 5.2 The net interest margin of retail banks is largely driven by a large inflow of funds due to stock market activities, which makes Hong Kong dollar liquidity more abundant. The aforementioned risk factors will continue to affect the credit quality and profitability of the banking sector in the near future. The capital of the Hong Kong banks sector remains sound and far exceeds the minimum international standards. The one-tier capital ratio for the period is 18.7%, of which 16.7% is common equity tier one (CET1) capital. Furthermore, the leverage ratio of the locally registered licensed institutions remained at a stable level of 8.2% at the late of December 2020, exceeding the statutory minimum level of 3% (Figure 5.6). The average liquidity coverage ratio for Category 1 institutions in the fourth quarter of 2020 was 155.1% (Figure 5.7), significantly exceeding the statutory minimum requirement of 100%. The novel coronavirus epidemic caused a massive impact on the global financial market in March 2020. During this period of market volatility, some open-end funds experienced significant capital outflows (Figure B1.1), posing a pressure on their liquidity management. Figure B1.1 During the period of events in March 2020, in addition to investor liquidity demands, another reason for the outflow of funds from some open-end funds was the large-scale withdrawal of funds by investors who adopted a "first-mover advantage" to redeem the fund early, thereby avoiding potentially surging redemption costs under conditions of pressure in the market. To curb capital outflows caused by the first-mover advantage, some open-end funds adopt swing pricing—a fund pricing rule that mitigates the first-mover advantage for investors. Although many open-end funds have used swing pricing in secondary events, there is no empirical research indicating whether swing pricing can effectively reduce the outflow of open-end funds. In this context, this study conducts an empirical investigation to understand whether swing pricing can reduce the outflow of capital from open-end funds during the events of March 2020, thereby lowering their liquidity risk. Furthermore, this study will also seek factors that may limit the effectiveness of swing pricing when the market is under pressure. Based on these assessments, we will propose policy recommendations regarding financial stability. First-mover advantage refers to investors redeeming earlier than other investors, thereby passing the redemption costs onto them. The first-mover advantage primarily exists in open-end funds that adopt traditional pricing rules, where the subscription and redemption costs for the fund's investors (such as transaction costs resulting from portfolio adjustments) are reflected in the open-end fund price after the transaction takes place. Under this pricing mechanism, investors redeeming shares shall not be subject to those transaction costs. This became the incentive for them to redeem the fund early, especially in the case of anticipated large redemption costs. Therefore, when the market is under pressure, the first-mover advantage will become more pronounced due to the expected increase in redemption costs. This expanded the redemption pressure and liquidity risk faced by open-end funds.

Climate change affects every aspect of life, and each individual has a responsibility to contribute to mitigating the impacts of climate change. Accordingly, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has invested significant effort in promoting Hong Kong's climate goals and is contributing to enhancing global climate change response capacity and sustainable development. Following last year when we included the first sustainable development report in the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's 2021 Annual Report as one chapter, this year we will publish the 2022 sustainable development report separately for the first time. I hope this report will allow readers to gain a deeper understanding of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's strategies and key focus areas regarding strengthening the capacity of the Hong Kong banks system to address Climate change, build a green financial ecosystem, and how to implement work strategies in areas such as responsible investment and sustainable development organizations. During the year, we have made significant progress in advancing the sustainable development work of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's key functions. Everyone will learn about our specific measures and work in this report, with the main points being the following: the daily operations of the banks face climate risks. As a banking regulatory body, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has taken specific measures to strengthen the capacity of banks to address Climate change. In 2022, we developed a two-year plan to incorporate climate risks into regulatory procedures and to research how to leverage the power of technology to assist banks in assessing the impact of entity risks. As banks are launching more and more green and sustainable products, we have also shared best practices on how to properly manage these products with the industry to promote banks' ability to strengthen their climate risks management. the Hong Kong Monetary Authority actively participates in cooperative programmes related to addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance development. Locally, we are collaborating with other financial regulatory bodies through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group" (Steering Group) to develop a local green classified framework. The framework will increase the transparency of the financial markets and make green financial policies more consistent. At the international level, we are actively participating in several different international organizations to assist in formulating policies to address Climate change and to assess its impact on financial stability. Hong Kong possesses the conditions to meet the Asia region's demand for green and sustainable financing. Although 2022 was a challenging year for the global bond market, the issuance amount of green and sustainable debt in Hong Kong continued to grow strongly, with an increase of 42%, bringing the total issuance to 80.5 billion dollar, making it the largest hub for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances in the Asia region². The relevant issuers include the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government and the Hainan Provincial People's Government, whose issuance again demonstrates Hong Kong's unique role in promoting green and sustainable financial flows between the mainland and international. The Hong Kong green bond market is thriving, partly attributable to the government's green bond programme. Since 2019, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has assisted the government in issuing green bonds valued at nearly 16 billion dollars, with the proceeds allocated to over 40 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recycling, energy efficiency, and energy saving. We also assisted the government in achieving a "first" in two areas, including assisting the government in issuing the first batch of government green retail bonds worth HK$20 billion in May 2022, which was the largest green retail bond issuance globally at that time. Additionally, we also assisted the government in issuing the first batch of tokenized green bonds in February 2023. This is the first issuance of tokenized green bonds issued by the government globally, and the subsequent issuance also marks a milestone in our successful integration of the advantages of the bond market, green and sustainable finance, and financial technology. Standards, data, and human resources are indispensable elements driving the sound development of the climate finance ecosystem, and this requires the efforts and cooperation of various sectors to be established. For this purpose, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority primarily cooperates with the Steering Group and other relevant government departments, regulatory bodies, academic institutions, and the financial industry to expand the aforementioned elements. In addition to the establishment of the local green classified framework mentioned above, the Steering Group also promotes skills training within the industry and improves Hong Kong's data resources through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Centre" established under its umbrella. Furthermore, the Steering Group has also made good progress in other areas such as the mandatory disclosure of climate-related information and carbon market opportunities. In 2022, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority further strengthened the work of foreign exchange funds in responsible investment, particularly by setting the target for foreign exchange fund investment portfolios to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. At the same time, we have also optimized risk management to enhance the climate response capability and risk-adjusted long-term returns of the foreign exchange funds. Furthermore, to fully seize the opportunities that climate change may bring, we are committed to promoting sustainable investment in foreign exchange funds, seeking investment opportunities that support climate transition and mitigate climate change, in order to enhance the long-term returns of the investment portfolio. By the end of 2021, the weighted average carbon density of the foreign exchange funds stock portfolio decreased by 43% compared to the level in 2017. In fact, foreign exchange funds continue to bear lower risk concerning high-carbon assets compared to the overall market. In the future, we will continue to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management process, actively exercise ownership, and continuously collaborate with all stakeholders, focusing on decarbonization and transformation of investment portfolios to continue moving towards net-zero emissions. At the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the "Institutional Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Committee," chaired by me, is responsible for formulating the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainable development strategy. Our strategic direction is based on the three pillars of environmental, employee, and social responsibility. In terms of the environmental aspect, we are committed to promoting a green working environment and promoting a more environmentally friendly market to the public. Regarding employees, as an employer responsible for and caring for employees, we actively cultivate a healthy and inclusive work environmental. In terms of social responsibility, we are committed to improving the public's financial knowledge level, promoting financial inclusion, and actively giving back to society. Compared to the levels when we began tracking carbon footprint in 2015, the per capita greenhouse gas emissions, energy consumption, and paper usage in 2022 have all achieved double-digit reductions. More importantly, we have developed a roadmap to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner. In the short term, our goal is to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions, and using 2015 as a baseline, to reduce Scope 2 emissions by 63% by 2030 or earlier to address climate change and promote sustainable development through continuous and ongoing efforts and cooperation from multiple parties. On this important global issue, we understand that it is necessary to take action through our conduct, and to work together with colleagues and international organizations who share the same principles. In the next section, we will outline the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's short-term plans and key priorities in addressing climate change under its major functions. Achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner is a formidable task, and we will exert our utmost effort to achieve this goal. We are confident that through the joint efforts of all colleagues, the financial industry, and the general public, we can successfully address future climate challenges. Chairman Yu Wei-wen

In 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to promote the sustainable development of the Hong Kong financial industry and fulfill its responsibilities as a responsible investor and a sustainability institution. Concurrently, through participation in international and regional organizations, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will also be committed to promoting the broad development and best practices of green and sustainable finance. As a regulator of the banking industry, we are committed to strengthening the climate resilience of the banking sector and further improving our green finance ecosystem to support the green transition of banks. Specifically, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will communicate with the banks to understand their progress in implementing climate risk management regulatory provisions, to incorporate climate factors into our regulatory review procedures, and to jointly assess the revision of the banking industry's "green standards" framework. Meanwhile, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will support banks in their work to enhance climate resilience and risk management capabilities, for example, by exploring different measures and technological solutions to help banks identify, calculate, and monitor their climate risk exposure. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will also collaborate with banks to conduct the next round of climate risk stress testing, as part of the regular stress testing led by the regulatory authority for the 2023 to 2024 fiscal year. Participating banks will be required to assess their ability to respond to climate risks according to the optimized stress testing framework. This framework encompasses various stress scenarios, including extreme climate and adverse economic conditions. To promote the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will closely follow local and international market and regulatory developments, and maintain communication with the industry to provide guidance on sales processes in a timely manner. We will also conduct on-site specialized assessments to fully understand the green and sustainable investment products offered by the banks. At the same time, to strengthen the construction of the green finance ecosystem to support the green transition of the financial industry, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is planning to consult the industry on the structure and core elements of developing a local green classified framework. In terms of market development, to promote Hong Kong as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will assist the government in expanding the issuance scale of green bonds under the "Government Green Bond Programme" and broadening the scope of the programme to include sustainable development bonds. Simultaneously, attract more green financing activities to take place in Hong Kong through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also assists in promoting the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme" to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to encourage more mainland local governments, institutions, and enterprises to conduct green financing through Hong Kong and explore the feasibility of combining green finance with technology. On the other hand, we will continue to cooperate with other organizational departments on cross-industry issues such as skills training and data, green classified directories, climate-related disclosures and sustainable reporting, as well as carbon market opportunities, through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group." Through the green commercial bank alliance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will jointly launch different specialized programs with international financial institutions in the Asia region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training to banks, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in formulating roadmaps to make green finance a core business. Looking to the future, the alliance will work closely with its foundational members, global partners, and knowledge partners to launch a membership program to expand the alliance's influence in the Asian region. The alliance will also strengthen and enhance the professional capabilities of industry personnel, promote the sharing of green finance knowledge, and lead the undertaking of project plans in new areas. As a responsible investor, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has set a goal for its foreign exchange fund investment portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, as a commitment to participate in the global climate response work and the climate-related financial disclosure working group's recommendations. Looking ahead, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to incorporate environmental, social, and governance factors into its investment management procedures, strive towards the net-zero emissions goal, and fully support global climate response efforts. As a responsible and sustainable organization, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is concerned not only with its employees but also with the public and the surrounding environment. We have developed a sustainability roadmap and established climate targets for our own operations, as a commitment to our participation in global carbon reduction and climate response efforts. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to prioritize reducing carbon emissions and encourage employees to fully support energy saving and waste reduction. Furthermore, we will provide further guidance to employees to incorporate sustainability principles into the procurement process. To implement digital transformation and enhance operational flexibility, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will explore methods for modernizing internal systems and applications to further improve work efficiency while minimizing potential risks that may arise during the digital transformation process.

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always been committed to consolidating the Hong Kong financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations. To continue to play its important function in the financial system and guide more capital towards green and sustainability projects, banks must proactively manage climate risk. As a banking regulatory body, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is particularly focused on building the capacity for banks to address climate risk and manage climate risk, and accelerating the work of banks to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also supports banks in enhancing their capabilities in detecting environmental crimes and participated in the recently published risk assessment for money laundering and terrorist financing in Hong Kong, which covers areas such as environmental crimes and illegal wildlife smuggling. In 2022, the Basel Committee issued effective principles for the management and supervision of climate-related financial risks and responded to common questions, clarifying how the existing Basel framework covers the aforementioned risks for banks. In response to these international developments, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to strive to incorporate climate-related factors into the regulatory framework. After issuing the "Regulatory Policy Manual" Unit GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" in 2021, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has also maintained communication with banks to exchange views on the expectations, progress, and challenges in implementing the relevant regulatory requirements. To further strengthen the supervision of Climate Risk Management in the banking sector, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has formulated a two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the supervision procedures of banks and communicated this to the banking industry in June. As part of the two-year plan implementation, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority issued the revised Chapter SA-1 of the Regulatory Policy Manual, "Risk-Based Supervision System," and enhanced the CAMEL2 rating system by incorporating climate risk into the risk-based supervision procedures. At the same time, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority improved the climate risk stress testing scenarios and assessment framework based on the experience gained from the pilot program since 2021. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has also formulated a plan to incorporate the next round of climate risk stress testing into regular stress tests led by regulatory bodies to conduct a more comprehensive assess of the resilience of the banking sector under extreme climate scenarios. Under the two-year plan, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is also strengthening its green assessment framework for banks to reflect the latest developments in sustainability-related issues (including Climate Risk Management and transition planning). At the same time, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is reviewing the supervisory review procedures for the second pillar capital requirements, which are used to assess and supervise the capital adequacy levels of banks, aiming to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address the risks related to Climate change and the transition to carbon neutrality. Given the increasing popularity of banks issuing green and sustainability products, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority conducted a special review, primarily examining the banks' development and ongoing management of these products. During the special review process, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority identified some good practices and issued a notice in December to share with the industry, encouraging banks to gradually strengthen their Climate Risk Management capabilities. Applied technology can improve data availability and strengthen the ability of banks to manage climate risk. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has begun developing a universal platform for banks to assess the impact of entity risk on real estate. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, in conjunction with other central banks and regulatory bodies, will undertake projects under the International Settlement Bank Innovation Network to explore how technological solutions can assist in physical risk assessment. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also places great importance on promoting sustainability and leading global anti-money laundering work practices. This aspect of the work employs advanced analytics and compliance technology, supplemented by fully automated regulatory data collection. In the past 12 months, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has streamlined the anti-money laundering regulatory data collection process to reduce the burden on banks and paper volume. To enhance transparency in the financial markets and to bring green financial policies into greater alignment, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is collaborating with other financial regulatory bodies to establish a local green classified framework. The green classification framework is generally known as the green classification directory, which classifies economic activities as green or sustainable, providing a reference for the authorities and market participants to determine whether a particular activity or its related products are truly green or sustainable. Therefore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will maintain contact with the industry and other relevant stakeholders to thoroughly explore the features and challenges of this framework, and prepare recommendations and conduct consultations on the structure and core elements of the framework in the first half of 2023. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is well aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; therefore, broader climate factors and scenarios should be incorporated into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current supervisory work. In the process of continuously monitoring financial stability risks, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will take into account climate change and include analyses of climate-related risks in all financial stability reports. Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis working group under the "central and regulatory institution green finance network" (NGFS), The Hong Kong Monetary Authority assists in further enriching climate scenarios, enabling the central bank and regulatory institutions to gain a clearer understanding of the impact of Climate change on the macroeconomy and finance. In terms of research work, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority conducted multiple applied research projects in 2022, deeply exploring two issues: the greenwashing behavior in the corporate green bond market3, and the role of disclosure in bearing climate risk4. The research findings above are helpful in formulating policies and regulatory measures to address the impact of climate risk on financial stability. Locally, this research helps strengthen The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's ongoing monitoring and assess of the impact of climate risk on financial stability. Externally, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has shared research findings with various stakeholders through various channels, including international central bank research seminars and the Authority's "Semi-annual Report on Currency and Financial Stability." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Liquidity Funding Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized reserve funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is studying the inclusion of sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and promoting sustainability in finance as the mainstream. Through participation in this area, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority helps promote policy dialogue internationally and regionally on addressing Climate change and its impact on financial stability, and to draw insights to enhance the climate adaptation capacity of the Hong Kong financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is intensifying efforts to enhance market awareness and participation, provide necessary infrastructure and drivers, and support international initiatives to align with global standards. The Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group (Steering Group) is jointly led by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission, responsible for coordinating the financial industry's response measures to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the government's climate strategy1. The work of the steering group is primarily based on its strategic plan, which outlines six key focus areas and five action plans to consolidate the Hong Kong financial ecosystem and build a greener and more sustainable future (Figure 1). Strengthen financial risk management related to climate, consolidate Hong Kong's position as a global risk management centre, promote the circulation of climate-related information at all levels to facilitate risk management, capital allocation, and investor protection, enhance the relevant skills of industry professionals, strengthen public awareness and understanding to encourage product innovation and research measures, guide capital flows towards green and sustainable projects to seize opportunities brought by Mainland China, and develop Hong Kong into a green finance centre for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (Greater Bay Area). Efforts to promote Hong Kong's sustainable finance development regionally and internationally to date: the steering group has made good progress since its establishment. The current focus of the steering group's work includes skills training and data collection under green and sustainable finance centers (see below), the green classified directory (see Chapter 9, "Establishing a Green Classification Framework to Promote Green Financial Flows" on page 9, "Building a Sustainable Financial System"), climate-related disclosures and sustainable reporting, and carbon market opportunities. Specifically, the steering group published a preliminary feasibility assessment of the carbon market opportunities in Hong Kong in March, and will support Hong Kong's development as a carbon trading hub in the region, including the development of high-quality international voluntary carbon markets and seizing the opportunities brought by Greater Bay Area cooperation. In December, the steering group announced a collaboration with CDP2 to enhance data availability in Hong Kong and strengthen sustainability reporting. As part of this cooperation, both parties will develop a climate and environmental risk questionnaire targeting unlisted companies and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which will both facilitate the company's sustainable development reporting and assist financial institutions in collecting and analyzing company-level data for risk assessment and related business decisions. This is an important step in the steering group expanding the scope of data work coverage to include the SME sector, an economic segment that was previously difficult to reach yet is important. The steering group established the green and sustainable finance centers in July 2021, responsible for coordinating the work of financial regulatory bodies, government departments, industry stakeholders, and academic institutions in training and policy formulation, and for establishing resources and databases. In the first half of 2022, the center launched three databases focusing on data, training information, and internship opportunities, assisting the financial industry and other sectors in accessing data and learning resources related to green and sustainable finance. The resource library provides data sources to aid the industry in training talent to assess the physical risks in Hong Kong; the center assisted the government in launching the "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme" in December, providing subsidies to employees, students, and graduates participating in training and skills enhancement related to green and sustainable finance. Other measures to promote skills training include launching the "Sustainable Finance Internship Program" to create more internship opportunities for students, and developing a new module 3 on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" for bank employees. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has consistently actively supported the development of Green and Sustainable Finance in the region through the Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme. In November 2020, the International Financial Corporation and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance," gathering financial institutions, banking industry organizations, research institutions, and innovative technology providers within the region to jointly develop a cooperative platform for green commercial banks. The alliance aims to enable commercial banks and other financial institutions to fully realize their potential, develop green finance as a mainstream core business, and promote the participation of the financial system in global climate change-related activities. The operating method is to provide a one-stop mutual learning platform for financial institutions to obtain the necessary knowledge, tools, and information to formulate their own green finance roadmap, and to transform into credible green finance institutions that gather green finance leaders, facilitate communication among green finance institutions in different emerging markets, and explore cutting-edge issues to drive the global green finance agenda, unlocking endless green and climate-related investment opportunities. In June, five global leading financial institutions became foundational members of The alliance and closely cooperated with the International Financial Corporation and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to encourage clients to adopt green strategies, promote best practices in green products and services, and unlock new business opportunities, thereby helping to realize the green economic transformation. In addition, three global partners and one knowledge partner committed in 2022 to provide climate expertise in areas such as innovation, standardization, and academic research. Details of the alliance and member structure are available on the relevant webpage (English version): The foundational members, the International Financial Corporation, and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority signed a Memorandum of Understanding. Furthermore, since March 2021, the alliance has jointly held 18 training activities and roundtable meetings, attracting over 6,000 participants from various global locations, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. Furthermore, The alliance, in June 2022, published its first cutting-edge research report titled "Climate Risk: Definition, Measurement, Current Practices, and Regulation" in collaboration with the Hong Kong Monetary and Financial Research Centre (Research Centre). The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has consistently promoted green and sustainable debt issuance and built an ecosystem of local relevant professional services. The total amount of green and sustainable debt issued in Hong Kong in 2022 (including bonds and loans) reached 80.5 billion dollar, an increase of 42%. The issuance of green and sustainable debt amounting to +42% (US$80.5 billion) demonstrates the government's commitment to addressing climate change, promoting green finance, and striving to develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city. In 2018, the government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme," and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority assisted in promoting the related green bond issuance. The government has issued nearly 16 billion dollar equivalent green institutional and retail bonds to date, with the raised funds allocated to over 40 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recycling, energy efficiency, and energy saving. To enhance the transparency of the plan and accountability arrangements, the government annually publishes the Green Bond Report, detailing the allocation of funds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. To enable citizens to participate in the outcomes of Hong Kong's sustainable development and sharing through investment, the first tranche of green retail bonds, with a total value of HK$20 billion, was issued in May and received enthusiastic support from citizens, becoming the largest green retail bond issued globally at that time. This issuance also expands the range of green and sustainable finance products in Hong Kong, consolidating Hong Kong's position as the leading green finance hub in the region and internationally. The government continued its regular green institutional bond issuance during the 2022 to 2023 fiscal year, and issued green bonds worth 5.75 billion dollar in January 2023. This is a tri-currency issuance covering the dollar, euro, and renminbi, with tenors ranging from 2 to 30 years, continuing to serve as an important benchmark for potential issuers in Hong Kong and the surrounding region. This issuance was widely welcomed by the global investment community and successfully attracted new investors who had not participated in previous green bond issuances by the government, reflecting investor confidence in Hong Kong's long-term credit situation and economic outlook. The government has increased the issuance amount of renminbi bonds to 10 billion renminbi in response to investor demand. The shareholding of international investors and Mainland China investors participating through the Bond Connect channel in this issuance has also increased, demonstrating Hong Kong's position as the primary offshore renminbi business hub and further solidifying Hong Kong's leadership status as an international financial center. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also assisted the government in issuing tokenized green bonds in February 2023 to test the use of distributed classified ledger technology for bond issuance and settlement. This is the first batch of tokenized green bonds issued by The government globally. This primary issuance will settle on a private blockchain network on a T+1 basis, and the subsequent processes (including coupon payments, secondary market transactions, and maturity redemption) will also be digitized. The experience of this issuance by the government can serve as a reference for market participants interested in issuing similar bonds in the future. To provide the industry with credible and convenient market information, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to cooperate with the Climate Bond Initiative and the International Capital Markets Association to separately issue annual reports on the green debt market in Hong Kong and the region. The report by the International Capital Markets Association shows that in 2022, Hong Kong became the largest hub in the Asia region for the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds, with the total amount of bonds issued through Hong Kong reaching 27.8 billion dollar, accounting for over one-third of the total in the region. The maximum issuance hub for international green and sustainable bonds in the Asia region, amounting to 27.8 billion dollar, followed the initial issuance in 2021, and the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government reissued 5 billion renminbi offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong in November 2022, including 2.6 billion renminbi green and blue bonds. The People's Government of Hainan Province also issued 5 billion renminbi offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time this month, including blue and sustainable bonds. The aforementioned bond issuance activities repeatedly highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable financing between Mainland China and the global regions, as well as its long-standing position as the premier fundraising platform in the region. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to promote and implement the "green and sustainable finance support scheme" launched in 2021, and utilizes this scheme to attract more relevant professional service providers (including financial institutions, green consulting firms, and external rating agencies) to establish and expand their operations in Hong Kong. This plan is widely welcomed by the industry. As of the end of 2022, the plan covered external review service expenses for issuers of green and sustainable debt instruments, including pre-issuance, post-issuance, or both, to help issuers ensure and demonstrate strict adherence to market best practices and international standards. Starting from March, the plan will be optimized, lowering the minimum loan amount threshold for applying for external review fee subsidies from HK$200 million to HK$100 million, which will assist smaller enterprises in obtaining green financing. Following the successful concept validation of tokenized retail green bonds under Project Genesis in 2021, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the International Settlement Bank Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre have collaborated again under Genesis 2.0 to explore the technical feasibility of digital carbon offsets (also known as Mitigation Outcome Incentives, abbreviated as MOI), thereby enhancing the transparency, objectivity, and green elements of the green bonds market. This project was completed in October 2022, successfully developing two prototypes to track, deliver, and transfer digital MOIs through the use of blockchain and other relevant technologies.

As one of the world's largest asset holders and managers, the Monetary Authority plays a significant role in promoting green and sustainable finance development to support the global climate change agenda. The Monetary Authority is also a pioneer of responsible investment, having led investments in green and sustainable assets since before 2015, requiring its external investment managers to adopt the "Principles for Responsible Ownership" issued by the Securities and Futures Commission, and to integrate environmental, social, and governance factors into the investment management of foreign exchange funds. The Monetary Authority prudently invests according to the principle of "preserve principal first, long-term appreciation," believing that emphasis on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors can unlock long-term sustainable value and mitigate related risks for investments. Facing increasingly severe climate change challenges, the Monetary Authority continues to advance on its responsible investment journey, including setting the "net-zero emissions by 2050" target in 2022 and optimizing risk management strategies to enhance the resilience of the asset portfolio, thereby securing more favorable risk-adjusted long-term returns for foreign exchange funds. The Monetary Authority is also actively involved in building a green and sustainable finance ecosystem, collaborating with investors and regulatory bodies with similar philosophies to promote responsible investment, and cooperating with international organizations to establish ESG investment standards. The transparency of climate-related information plays a significant role in managing climate risks. To fulfill its commitment to support the green finance network (NGFS) for the central bank and regulatory bodies, as outlined in the Glasgow Declaration issued at the 2021 UN Climate Change Conference and the commitment to greening the global financial system, the Monetary Authority has made climate-related disclosures for foreign exchange funds in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) under the purview of the Financial Stability Board. a. FCLTGlobal — Focusing Capital on the Long Term b. PRI — Principles for Responsible Investment c. NGFS — central and regulatory bodies green finance network d. TCFD — Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures The Chairman of the Ministry of Finance established the responsible investment framework and guiding principles for the foreign exchange funds advisory committee, and this is implemented in the investment management of the foreign exchange funds by the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office. The primary guiding principle is for the Monetary Authority to prioritize ESG investments with risk-adjusted long-term returns comparable to other assets to implement the investment objectives of the foreign exchange funds. Details regarding the Monetary Authority's responsible investment framework can be found on the Monetary Authority website: The Investment Committee under the Foreign Exchange Funds Advisory Committee is chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority and is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks associated with foreign exchange funds investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policy, and through regular meeting reports from the Risk Management and Supervision Department of the foreign exchange funds investment office, monitors the progress of integrating ESG factors into investments and the ESG status of the foreign exchange funds. As shown in Figure 1, the ESG committee established under the foreign exchange funds investment office is chaired by the Chief Risk Officer and is responsible for coordinating and supervising all ESG work of the foreign exchange funds investment office. The agenda items and progress of work discussed by the ESG Committee at each meeting will be reported to the CEO of the foreign exchange funds investment office. The dedicated team of the Risk Management and Supervision Department and the various investment teams of the foreign exchange funds investment office collaborate closely on integrating ESG factors, and assist the senior management of the foreign exchange funds investment office in managing the ESG and climate-related risks and opportunities of various investment projects: Public market investments are monitored by the credit, compliance, and supervisory committees composed of senior management of the foreign exchange funds investment office through regular reports from the Risk Management and Supervision Department regarding the ESG status of fixed-income asset portfolios. Furthermore, the Risk Management and Supervision Department also participates in the selection, appointment, and supervision process of external investment managers for stock portfolios from an ESG perspective (see the section "Actively exercising ownership rights" in the "Risk Management" section on page 27). The Investment Committee, chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority, will consider the ESG-related assess made by the Risk Management and Supervision Department and the private market investment team for each investment recommendation in private market investments. Specific evidence further shows the significant impact of climate change and related risks. According to the latest report 3 of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (the Climate Change Convention), even if the nationally determined contributions announced by each region are fully implemented, the estimated global temperature increase by 2100 will still reach 2.1 to 2.4 degrees Celsius, making it difficult to achieve the goal of limiting the global average temperature increase under the Paris Agreement to below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. If regions adopt more progressive policy measures to narrow the temperature gap, the transition risk⁴ and the repricing of assets by the market based on anticipated future trends, coupled with inherent physical risks, will all exacerbate the pressure on asset valuations. In view of the trajectory of global warming and the update of model assumptions, the Monetary Authority, leveraging the specialized knowledge of external consultants, further assesses the resilience of the "portfolio" of foreign exchange funds under the "rapid transformation" scenario (Figure 2), following the assessment conducted in 2021. The "rapid transformation" scenario includes higher transition risk factors in the short, medium, and long term, assuming that policy changes and technological development jointly cause a rapid decrease in carbon emissions, while various assets are suddenly divested to maintain the average temperature increase before 2100 within 1.5 degrees Celsius. The disorderly scenarios suggested by the forward-looking climate impact assess for the scenario and NGFS are largely consistent. The portfolio can maintain resilience in the medium to long term because the larger proportion of the assets allocation consists of sovereign bonds, which are less sensitive to transformation. Industry distribution is key. Low-carbon power and renewable energy assets can benefit from the relevant transition. Transition risk and the repricing of assets may have an impact on performance in the short term (especially equity assets). The overall portfolio will be increasingly affected by physical risks that gradually emerge over time. Energy and traditional utilities remain the most susceptible industries. The climate scenario and other modeling methods have their limitations. The analysis is based on the market benchmark industry distribution at the strategic assets allocation level and does not consider the effect of actively selecting specific securities within a particular industry. From more in-depth research, it is evident that investment items within a portfolio generally are better able to withstand transition shocks or suffer less impact compared to the market benchmark of strategic assets allocation. This result again affirms that the Monetary Authority's focus on responsible investment to counter climate change can enhance the resilience of asset portfolios. The trajectory of climate change remains unclear, and scenario analysis methods will continue to evolve with improvements in data quality and policy development. The Monetary Authority regularly reviews relevant scenarios and optimizes the assess to more clearly confirm the resilience of foreign exchange funds to climate change. As a long-term investor, the Monetary Authority fully understands the risks and opportunities that climate change may bring. The Monetary Authority is committed to further expanding sustainable investment and seizing opportunities to address climate transition, mitigate climate risks, and enhance the long-term returns of asset portfolios. The Monetary Authority continued its good momentum in 2022, increasing the holdings of green, social, and sustainable bonds by another fifty percent. In terms of stock investment, the Monetary Authority invests in active stock portfolios with a governance theme, and adopts a decarbonization strategy focused on low-carbon emitting companies for passive stock portfolios. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority is discussing with the managers of the "long-term growth portfolio" of the foreign exchange funds the establishment of a dedicated private equity fund to promote green and sustainable development in the Asia region (Figure 3). Figure 3: Continued promotion of measures to increase ESG investment. The Monetary Authority has invested in the operation of an African-wide wind power generator, and in addition to producing clean energy, the operator also places great importance on social and biodiversity factors. Before the wind farm was established, local villagers used poisoned bait to prevent predatory animals from preying on their livestock, but this action inadvertently harmed certain endangered species of bald eagles. Livestock are important assets of the local villagers, and to assist the villagers in protecting their livestock, the operator has built livestock shelters within the wind farm to protect the livestock from predation by natural predators. Furthermore, the operator employs a sparrow surveillance team to issue warnings when bald eagles are attracted by animal carcasses incidentally left by predators, in order to shut down wind turbines and prevent the eagles from being struck by the blades. Reducing the situation where livestock are preyed upon brings a win-win outcome: on one hand, it secures the livelihoods of the villagers, and on the other hand, it reduces the incidence of bald eagles being struck and killed by wind turbines, thereby protecting endangered species. Good ESG practices can bring more business opportunities to companies and open up revenue streams; the supply chain operations below are one example. The investment company is an integrated logistics warehousing operator in China, specializing in cold chain medical, chemical products, and high-end consumption logistics services. The company faces continuously increasing ESG operating standards, primarily from multinational corporate clients requiring their service providers to meet the high carbon reduction targets aligned with the Paris Agreement. In response to the relevant demands, the company has engaged an external consultant to assist in developing a "Three-Year ESG Plan" to reduce carbon emission intensity by 50% by 2030 or earlier. This comprehensive decarbonization plan has already yielded significant results in 2021. The aforementioned ESG measures have earned the company the "low-carbon green management case" award from the China Logistics and Procurement Association. These achievements and accolades enable the company to gain considerable business opportunities from multinational clients who particularly value ESG practices in the consumption and chemical products sectors. The growth of ESG investment is closely related to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. The Monetary Authority actively cooperates with investors and partners who share similar philosophies, promoting responsible investment and enhancing industry skills. The Monetary Authority successfully hosted the 4th annual ESG workshop in 2022, facilitating exchanges on good ESG practices among nine participating private market institutions (including managing partners, limited partners, and corporations), and promoting sustainable investment opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region and the Greater Bay Area. In the public market, the Monetary Authority urges trading partners (mainly investment banks) to expand their ESG personnel and research capabilities, particularly in Hong Kong. Mr. Li Da-zhi, CEO of the foreign exchange funds investment office, delivered the opening remarks at the Monetary Authority's ESG workshop in 2022 on an international level. The Monetary Authority is actively involved in formulating industry ESG investment standards and practices: as one of the earliest central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the Monetary Authority participated in the joint action of signatories coordinated by the PRI to develop a uniform responsible investment due diligence questionnaire for private market investments in private equity and venture capital, Nos. 5 and 6, to assist private market investors in assess the ESG of managing partners and investment recommendations. The Monetary Authority participates in several working groups to support the research work of FCLTGlobal. This research aims to explore the main operational methods of the market for decarbonizing private assets within long-term portfolios, and the application of these methods for long-term investors. The Monetary Authority, as a member of NGFS and a supporter of TCFD, authored the NGFS's "Central Bank Climate-Related Disclosures Guidance" to demonstrate the Monetary Authority's commitment to adopting good ESG practices for banks and central banks. The Monetary Authority, in conjunction with the working group established under NGFS's "central bank net-zero emissions" initiative, has established a working group to participate in formulating the sustainable and responsible investment policies for the central banks. The Monetary Authority continues to participate in various industry forums and lectures, sharing insights on responsible investment and climate change strategies. Ms. Liu Huijuan, Chief Risk Officer of the foreign exchange funds investment office, spoke at the ESG investment opportunities sharing session, stating that building internal capabilities is crucial for continuing to advance the ESG journey. In addition to encouraging employees to take relevant courses in sustainable development and obtain relevant qualifications, the Monetary Authority also drew relevant knowledge and practical experience from the process of receiving advice on the main industry practices for the climate transition of asset portfolios from external consultants since 2021. On the other hand, the Monetary Authority utilizes ESG data compiled by a reputable external information provider to supplement its ongoing analysis of asset portfolios, in order to strengthen the ESG resilience of the foreign exchange funds.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to reducing its own institutional carbon footprint with the objective of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner, and to contribute to achieving Hong Kong's overall climate goals. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority strives to promote environmental sustainability on one hand, and fulfills its commitment to caring for employee physical and mental health, encouraging financial inclusion, and fulfilling social responsibility on the other. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to conducting daily operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. Therefore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority implements the concept of sustainable development under the three pillars of environment, employees, and social responsibility (Figure 1). The institutional social responsibility and sustainable development committee is responsible for leading the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in formulating and implementing sustainable development strategies. The committee is chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and its members include three deputy governors, as well as representatives from the Risk Management and Supervision Department and the Institutional Development and Operations Department. And submit periodic reports to the governing committee under the jurisdiction of the foreign exchange fund advisory committee. Under the leadership of the committee, multiple different teams and working groups are responsible for planning and executing the measures within their respective scopes. In 2022, the institutional social responsibility and sustainable development committee approved the institution's climate goals for operations and reviewed the transition roadmap to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the committee will continue to review the progress of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's green measures, including recommendations to strengthen the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainable development procurement policies, procedures, and methods. The governance framework for sustainable development; the journey of sustainable development of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is an acknowledgment of the Monetary Authority's commitment to the environment, employees, and society as a whole, with the Hong Kong Social Services Association presenting the "15 Years + Together in Care" emblem to The Hong Kong Monetary Authority for the 16th consecutive year. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority pays close attention to its own organization's carbon footprint and has established an internal "Green Office Guidelines" to control the environmental impact of operational procedures. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has integrated environmental factors into the office's interior design, operations, and maintenance and repair. In 2022, "Green Building Environmental Assessment" was granted a Gold certification by The Hong Kong Monetary Authority for certain office premises undergoing renovation. This is the second green building certification obtained after receiving Gold certification from LEED in 2021. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is implementing multiple energy-saving measures in the 1.0 version of the in-room building for the "Green Building Environmental Assessment." In 2022, the total energy consumption was 4,996.4 GWh (2.8 MWh per person), a decrease of 24.4% compared to 2015 (Figure 1). The total greenhouse gas emissions for Scope 1 and Scope 2 in 2022 were 8,299.64 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per person), a decrease of 38.2% compared to 2015 (Figure 2). Figure 1 Figure 2 Greenhouse gas emission density (Scope 1 and 2) The Hong Kong Monetary Authority encourages paperless operations within organizations. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority implements a printing management system, requiring employees to log into the printer to confirm each printing requirement, which helps reduce unnecessary printouts and toner usage. If printing is indeed required, double-sided paper and black and white printing are encouraged. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is also preparing to implement an internal electronic record-keeping system. The total paper consumption in 2022 was 20.5 metric tons (0.0114 metric tons per person), a decrease of 65.3% compared to 2015 (Figure A). Figure A: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to implement the "4R" principles for waste management. In addition to traditional waste, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also reduces electronic waste by adopting technological solutions such as server virtualization and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority first engaged an external company to audit waste and analyze the composition of waste generated by the office. This audit found that a large proportion of kitchen waste constitutes a significant part of the total waste, prompting The Hong Kong Monetary Authority to launch a kitchen waste recycling scheme (see page 41 "Enhanced Waste Management"). The total amount of non-hazardous waste generated in 2022 (including general waste and recyclable waste) was 242.0 tons (0.135 tons per person), a decrease of 4.8% compared to 2015 (Figure 3). The fluctuation in trends is mainly due to the implementation of work-from-home arrangements during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and the resumption of office operations after the fifth wave of the epidemic. Figure 3 Density of non-hazardous waste, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority prioritizes source reduction, and is committed to reducing use, reuse, and recycling. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority first engaged a company for audit waste in 2022 to more clearly understand the composition of waste in daily operations (plastics, paper, metal, glass, wood, electronic products, etc.) and to provide waste reduction recommendations. According to the audit results, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched the kitchen waste recycling scheme in November, installing kitchen waste collection bins in all pantry areas. Kitchen waste collected daily will be transported to an organic resource recycling center in Hong Kong and converted into renewable energy for power generation. The residue generated during the conversion process can also be made into compost for landscape beautification and agricultural production. Furthermore, trash cans are provided in different locations within the office for convenience. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority shares recycling tips with employees and focuses further on improving the source separation of recyclables, as well as precautions for handling recyclable items such as cardboard boxes, food containers, and beverage bottles. Furthermore, we continue to organize activities to raise employees' environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage employees to make good use of the recycling facilities in the office. Kitchen waste collected daily is transported to the organic resource recycling center for the recycling of plastics. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has two data centers (one for operation and one for backup). Since these two components account for the majority of the institution's overall energy consumption, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has implemented green design and multiple energy-saving measures, including cabinet-type air conditioning systems, light-emitting diode lighting equipment, and 24-hour monitoring of power efficiency. Following the advisory research on the green performance of the aforementioned data centers completed in 2022, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is preparing to implement recommendations to enhance overall energy efficiency. Preparations are also beginning for obtaining green data center certification. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority understands the importance of establishing a culture of sustainable development, and therefore regularly launches various programs and activities to educate and encourage employees to develop habits favorable to sustainable development and adopt green and digital working methods. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority shares green living tips with employees, as well as annual energy and paper consumption statistics for the entire office, reminding them to help address environmental matters at the individual level. Furthermore, employees are also encouraged to submit suggestions regarding sustainable development matters. Under the leadership of the Senior Manager of the Administration Department, a special team gathered employees from different departments to brainstorm and propose ideas and specific measures to promote a green work environment. Members of the special team also bear the responsibility of ambassadorship when launching new green measures. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority encourages the wider society to adopt more environmentally friendly operational methods and has introduced various measures to improve the operational efficiency of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the financial industry, and the overall economy, thereby minimizing resource consumption. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Electronic Submission Reporting System" (STET) is a one-stop platform that allows banks to submit documents to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority electronically, covering various periodic reports required weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annually. Another "e-Delivery" is a secure electronic communication channel that allows The Hong Kong Monetary Authority to send notices and guidance, etc., to the banks. Both systems help save a large amount of paper every year. In handling bank complaints and enforcement work, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has taken measures to support paperless submission of documents, and bank customers can make complaints through electronic channels and by filling out online forms. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is also developing a new generation management information systems to promote complaint handling and the transition from paper records to digital records. To reduce paper use, the Central Securities Clearing System (CMU)9 has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with its participants, including issuing notices, account opening and account termination letters, and responding to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, CMU will continue to explore more green measures, including the adoption of automated electronic procedures for internal and external communication. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority encourages the public to adopt more electronic payment methods, replacing cash and physical cheques, by promoting the use of the fast payment systems "ZhuanShuKua" and stored-value payment tools. For more information regarding "ZhuanShuKua" and value-added payment instruments, please refer to the chapter "Hong Kong's Position as an International Financial Centre" in the The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's 2022 Annual Report. Distributing electronic remittances is simple and convenient, and can reduce the use of physical remittance envelopes and banknotes, helping to promote sustainable development in Hong Kong. Therefore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to actively promote on various social platforms and traditional platforms, encouraging citizens to distribute e-gifts via online or mobile banking services using "ZhuanShuKua" or other e-wallet services through banks during the Lunar New Year. Major banks and e-wallet operators also host various activities to attract users to use e-gifts, such as providing user interfaces with a New Year atmosphere, enhancing functions for greater convenience, and launching prize draws or cash rebates. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority promotes e-gifts on social platforms for citizens who choose to distribute physical gifts during the Lunar New Year, and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to encourage them to use "Ying Xin Chao," which refers to using old yet new banknotes for sealing e-gifts. Ying Xin Chao can reduce the need for printing new banknotes, thereby decreasing the impact on the environment. Feedback from issuing banks indicates that citizens have increasingly accepted "Ying Xin Chao" in recent years. The coin collection scheme reflects the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's efforts in promoting coin recycling. Coins collected through this program will be returned to the market to meet public demand, improve the efficiency of coin circulation, and reduce the need for minting. The program has two collection vehicles and has served over one million people, collecting a total of over 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately 1.3 billion Hong Kong dollars. In 2022, approximately 78% of users chose to use some or all of their holdings as value-added to stored-value payment tools accounts. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Hong Kong Social Services Association have always maintained cooperation, deploying collection vehicles to collect coins from non-governmental organizations, dedicated to supporting social services. The coin collection program on the collection vehicles was launched in 2014, being the first systematic coin collection program globally to adopt the mobile vehicle concept, and has received multiple Hong Kong and international awards over the years for its innovative and environmentally friendly coin handling methods. The program has two collection vehicles, each equipped with two high-speed coin counting machines to collect the coins exchanged by the public. The public may choose to exchange coins for banknotes, use them to add value to stored-value payment tools accounts (such as a Datatong card or e-wallet), or donate them to public welfare funds as charity. In addition to collecting coins, collection vehicles are also sometimes assigned to be used for various educational activities (such as student tours).

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency independently verifies the climate targets of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). Climate targets are established in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Handbook ("SBTi Corporate Handbook"). The purpose of this verification work is to verify whether the climate targets have been established in accordance with the SBTi Corporate Handbook. This verification work is conducted in accordance with the "International Verification Engagement Guidelines 3000" (Revised Edition) issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provision for "Verification engagements other than the audit or review of historical financial data." The verification procedure is designed to make opinions and summaries to obtain a reasonable degree of assurance. The verification process is determined according to the requirements of the SBTi corporate handbook. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and summarizes: • The climate targets are established in reference to the SBTi corporate handbook. Shen Xiaoyin reviewed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency's March 2023 verification statement regarding the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency's independent verification of the 2022 environmental data ("2022 data") for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2022 data include the total energy consumption for 2022, the emission density of Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gases, the paper consumption density, the density and recycling rate of non-hazardous waste generated, and the changes in this data compared to the 2015 level. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emission data are compiled according to the GHG Protocol, a greenhouse gas accounting system developed jointly by the World Resources Institute ("WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development ("WBCSD"). The scope of verification covers data from January 1, 2022, to December 31, 2022, and also includes relevant data used for comparison of annual performance from January 1, 2015 level to December 31, 2015 level. The scope of verification includes a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, with 4 offices located in 1) International Finance Centre Phase II office, 2) Harmony Centre, 3) Tak Shing Plaza Phase I, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 2 warehouses in 5) Lecoq Industrial Centre and 6) Chongli Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan, respectively. The purpose of this verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and support evidence selected from 6 assets. This verification work is conducted in accordance with the "International Verification Engagement Guidelines 3000" (Revised Edition) issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provision for "Verification engagements other than the audit or review of historical financial data." The verification procedure is designed to make opinions and summaries to obtain a reasonable degree of assurance. The verification process is determined according to the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The validation process involved tracing the selected sample data back to its source to test the integrity and accuracy of the data, as well as reviewing the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducting reliability testing. The verification process also includes verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, visiting representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 data, and auditing representative data and information. The relevant original data and support evidence have also undergone detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team did not participate in the data preparation process for 2022. Based on the results of this verification, The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The 2022 data is substantially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Supervisor, The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023

Expanding and accelerating climate action has become the most urgent issue currently. Almost half of the key decade for the climate crisis has passed. We need to reduce global carbon emissions by over 40% in the next decade to have a chance of keeping the global warming level within 1.5 degrees Celsius. However, greenhouse gas emissions continue to reach new highs. The latest climate science research indicates that the window of opportunity to control the global temperature rise within 1.5 degrees Celsius will soon disappear. Everyone has clearly felt the impact of the 1.1-degree Celsius temperature rise—record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding, and storms, etc., extreme weather events are occurring frequently in global locations and are becoming more severe with each occurrence. Hong Kong was no exception; in September last year, after experiencing a fierce super typhoon, it was immediately followed by a century-scale torrential rain. Although we possess good infrastructure and can respond to disasters quickly, the impact remains very severe—flooding in wide areas, transportation disruptions, and damage to roads in many places. All these clearly remind us that decisive and proactive climate action is urgently required. Asia faces particularly significant challenges on the path to low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development and sustainability. We require a credible transition strategy that can appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means an easy task. Due to the rapid economic development within the region and the rapid population increase, its carbon emissions account for more than half of the global total emissions. Furthermore, the Asia-Pacific region has a high population density, and due to its geographical location, it is also susceptible to the effects of sea-level rise and extreme weather. Due to the uneven development progress of economies within the region, while the low-carbon transition will bring new opportunities to some economies, raising the necessary transition funds presents a significant challenge for others. Market estimates that the annual investment funds required for the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region over the next 30 years will exceed 3 trillion dollar. As an international financial center, Hong Kong possesses the capability and the responsibility to utilize financial power to support the low-carbon transition across the entire Asia region.
