As a regulator, market facilitator, and responsible investor in the banking industry, the Monetary Authority has consistently made significant efforts towards the sustainable development agenda. Everyone can learn about the various specific measures and work introduced by the Monetary Authority over the past year from each chapter of this report. Furthermore, to strengthen the internal governance structure of the Monetary Authority and to more effectively coordinate the sustainable development work across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee last year. For detailed information regarding the Supervisory Committee, please refer to the new chapter on "Sustainable Governance." Banks in Hong Kong play an important role in supporting the transition to net-zero emissions in Asia. In addition to fulfilling the traditional functions of banking regulatory bodies, we play a facilitator role in daily supervision by ensuring banks properly manage climate risks, and support the banking industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green classified framework to assist banks and other financial institutions in identifying environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype of the green classified framework for consultation in May, and are currently optimizing the framework based on the feedback collected during the consultation period. Furthermore, in response to the increasing demand from various sectors for higher quality and globally comparable sustainable disclosure information, the Monetary Authority is collaborating with other regulatory bodies to devise a clear roadmap for Hong Kong, adopting the disclosure guidelines released by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June, which constitute a comprehensive global sustainability reporting baseline for this task. The Monetary Authority's role as a facilitator is not limited to establishing frameworks and regulations; we are also committed to resolving pain points at the industry interface. Currently, many banks are limited by data and find it difficult to conduct physical risk assessment. In view of this, the Monetary Authority will launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform in the short term, allowing banks to simply input property addresses to assess the impact of physical disasters on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, thereby assisting banks in managing related climate risks. As a major international financial center and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has consistently played the role of a bridge, guiding international investment towards sustainable development projects in the region, supporting the low-carbon transition within the region. In recent years, the total amount of international green and sustainable bonds issued in Hong Kong has accounted for over one-third of the Asia market, clearly leading other regions. It is particularly noteworthy that the Shenzhen municipal government and the Hainan provincial government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong for the third and second consecutive years in 2023, again affirming Hong Kong's important role as a green gateway connecting the mainland with other global regions. Sustainable bond activities in Hong Kong are flourishing, partly attributable to the exemplary role of the "Government Green Bond Programme." Since 2019, the Monetary Authority has assisted the government in issuing green bonds valued at approximately 25 billion dollar, sold to institutional and retail investors. We seize every issuance opportunity, continuously innovating and expanding the features of green bonds, including currency, maturity, and distribution channels, to lay the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers within the region. Following the issuance of the largest government retail green bonds globally in 2022, we issued the first batch of tokenized government green bonds globally in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the issuance of the second tranche of tokenized green bonds. This batch of bonds is denominated in four major currencies and issued in a digital native format, making it the first global multi-currency digital green bonds. At the same time, we are also proactively introducing various measures to enhance the vitality and competitiveness of the sustainable finance ecosystem in Hong Kong. This encompasses work in various areas including skills training, data improvement, green fintech, and transformative finance. Specifically in talent training, in 2023, we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the professional qualifications framework of the banks, providing systematic courses for bank employees to enhance their understanding and professional knowledge of green and sustainable finance. Transformative finance is another key area of our work, providing funds for carbon reduction activities in high-carbon emission and hard-to-abate industries, preventing these industries from failing to transform due to a lack of financial support. To support the stable development of transformative finance, the Monetary Authority will expand the Hong Kong green classified framework to encompass transformative activities. We will also expand the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Support Scheme" for eligible bond issuers and borrowers to include transition bonds and loans, to encourage businesses within the region to raise transition funds in Hong Kong. Furthermore, we will strengthen communication and liaison with relevant stakeholders, attracting private sector investment into sustainable development projects that were previously difficult to finance through public-private partnerships and hybrid financial models. The aforementioned tasks require cross-sectoral cooperation, and the Green and Sustainable Finance inter-agency steering group, co-chaired by the Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission, will coordinate. Regional cooperation is also equally important. In addition to our long-term cooperation with international financial institutions on the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance," the Monetary Authority's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office also joined the "Sustainable Investment Capability Building Alliance" and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership" in 2023, becoming a founding member. Furthermore, the "Glasgow Net Zero Finance Alliance" has also announced plans to establish a branch in Hong Kong. This is a professional financial document; keep terminology precise and style consistent. Through these cooperative relationships, This hope to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, and subsequently support directing funds to sustainable development projects within the region and in global locations. To promote new business development and knowledge exchange, the Monetary Authority also assisted in hosting the inaugural "Hong Kong Green Week" earlier this year, attracting over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 regions, including top decision-makers in the global business and finance sectors, to jointly discuss solutions for expanding climate finance within the region and to establish new cooperative relationships. Chairman Mr. Yu Wai-man delivered a speech at the focal activities "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum" of the "Hong Kong Green Week," stating that the Monetary Authority, as the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a global important asset holder, should set an example by being a responsible investor. Since 2015, the Monetary Authority has been leading green and sustainable asset investment, and gradually expanding the scope of foreign exchange funds in ESG and green asset portfolios in both public and private markets. In line with the foreign exchange fund's objective to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, the Monetary Authority added a new active global equity investment portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition last year, while also expanding the application of a customized low-carbon stock index to another public market asset portfolio. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority prioritizes investment in green, social responsibility, and sustainable development bonds, which outperform the investment benchmark, demonstrating the principle of "doing good and getting rich." In the private market, we continue to pursue green-related investment opportunities and have become anchor investors for two transformation investment funds focused on Asia. At the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon density (WACI) of the foreign exchange fund stock portfolio decreased by 6% and 46% compared to the levels in 2021 and 2017, respectively, and has remained below the overall market level. The Monetary Authority, as a sustainable development organization, will continue to strive for progress and formulate our sustainable development goals and plans based on the three pillars of environment, employees, and social responsibility. Specifically, the Monetary Authority, in the journey of the low-carbon transition, continuously strengthens our capacity to address climate change by assessing our performance in the environment and implementing different internal measures. This measures cover emission reduction, energy efficiency improvement, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of achieving our commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner. We have formulated a plan to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the short term and have made good progress towards the medium-term goal of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030 years. To attract and retain excellent talent, in fulfilling the Monetary Authority's various important functions, in addition to green objectives, the Monetary Authority is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of employees. Furthermore, we contribute to creating a caring society by collaborating with various stakeholders to promote financial inclusion, enhance the financial literacy of citizens, and raise public awareness of financial fraud prevention. The climate challenge is enormous and extremely urgent. Economies in global locations are moving towards a more sustainable future, a process that is expected to bring significant changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries considerable risk, but will also bring unprecedented opportunities. As this global major sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in action to address these challenges. At the same time, we are also in a favorable position to ride the momentum. The Monetary Authority will fully support the industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. Continuing as a responsible investor and sustainable organization, putting into practice and collaborating with like-minded partners in line with the principles, to advance this currently very important global agenda. Chairman Yu Wei-wen

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are all related to the global. The Monetary Authority's objective in sustainable development work is to exert leadership through its own policies and operations to ensure that the Hong Kong financial system and the Monetary Authority itself can withstand the risks of climate change and support the transition to a more sustainable economic development. By actively participating in international and regional organizations, the Monetary Authority will also be committed to participating in the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards from the regional to the global level. As the regulatory body for the banking industry, the Monetary Authority will further strengthen the climate response and climate risk management capabilities of the banks. Specifically, the primary tasks include: launching a new round of thematic reviews and a new round of consultation meetings regarding the banks' climate risk management practices, as part of reviewing the progress of the banks in implementing climate risk management regulatory provisions. Continue the work on incorporating climate factors into the supervisory review procedures of the Monetary Authority. Completed the second round of industry-wide climate risk stress testing, and provided guidance to participating banks throughout the process, as well as sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry. To strengthen sustainability disclosures, including cooperation with local authorities to align relevant regulations with the international financial reporting standards for sustainability disclosures as a global benchmark, and to prepare for the third pillar 1 framework of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision for implementing climate-related financial risks for banks; and guidance on the best practices for sharing transformation plans with the industry. To promote the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the Monetary Authority will continue to closely follow local and international market and regulatory developments, and maintain contact with the industry to ensure banks adopt appropriate sales practices. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority will also play a facilitator role, striving to promote the development of the green financial ecosystem and support banks in providing financing for economic transformation. We will soon release the local green classified catalog and continue to expand its coverage to include more activities such as transformation activities. At the same time, we will also continue to explore the application of technological solutions to assist banks in identifying, quantifying, and monitoring their climate risk exposures. One example is the soon-to-be-launched cloud platform, which will promote the assessment of banks' physical risks. To enhance the professional capabilities of employees, we will also develop a professional-level module in "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" in 2024. Hong Kong possesses superior conditions as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfill this role, the Monetary Authority is assisting the government in implementing the proposals in the 2023-2024 "Fiscal Budget Proposal," expanding the scope of the "Government Green Bond Programme" to include sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market. Simultaneously, by attracting more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme." We will also continue to encourage more government, institutions, and enterprises to raise green finance through Hong Kong and explore the potential synergy between green finance and technology. Furthermore, we will continue to assist in promoting the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme" to expand the talent pool for green finance in Hong Kong. As the Co-Chair of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group" (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and work promoting the development of Green and Sustainable Finance in Hong Kong. The Steering Group will focus on three areas of work in 2024, including sustainable disclosure, the application of technology, and transformative finance. As another work focus, through the "Green Commercial Banks Alliance," the Monetary Authority and international financial institutions will continue to jointly launch different specialized programs in the Asia region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training to banks, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in supporting financial institutions to establish their distinctive green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also be committed to deepening cooperation with the "Glasgow Net-Zero Finance Alliance," the "Continuous Investment Capacity Building Alliance," and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership." As a responsible investor, the Monetary Authority commits the foreign exchange fund's "portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions targets by 2050 or sooner. We will continue to strengthen the sustainability of foreign exchange fund investments through a comprehensive and responsible investment approach, ensuring the resilience of the asset portfolio on the path toward net zero. We deeply understand that achieving the overall economic transformation is necessary to reach the goals of the Paris Agreement; therefore, we are optimizing our net zero strategy, focusing on assets that bring positive climate benefits to the real economy while considering the objectives of foreign exchange fund investments. As an organization that supports environmental protection, the Monetary Authority's decarbonization strategy will continue to keep pace with developments in the market, regulation, technology, and other climate-related areas. To further strengthen the Monetary Authority's climate response capabilities and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology-based solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our office. Furthermore, we will continue to actively encourage employees to participate in our sustainability initiatives, including launching promotional activities to foster sustainable habits and optimizing office processes and practical methods. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority will continue to maintain consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement methods, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices when selecting and renewing contracts. Based on obtaining green data center certification in 2023, the Monetary Authority pledges to adhere to the specified certification standards. Regarding the regular updates of data center facilities, in addition to keeping pace with the latest technology developments, we will also incorporate green design and operational methods. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and recycling, and actively modernize internal systems to improve efficiency and minimize potential risks. Finally, in terms of social focus, the Monetary Authority will seek out more community service opportunities for colleagues, cooperate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and raise financial literacy levels, and enhance public awareness of financial fraud prevention.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating these impacts. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and the wider Asia region through its multiple roles as a central bank institution, a regulator of the banking industry, a market facilitator, a responsible investor, and a sustainability institution. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has a sound sustainable development governance framework that leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Supervise the implementation of relevant measures, and ensure that the operations and working methods of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority incorporate sustainable development factors. To strive for good corporate governance, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has established a sound sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for related work. The governance framework ensures that the strategic planning and decision-making process of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority effectively integrates sustainability factors, and establishes effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and outcomes of sustainability work. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainability governance framework includes: the Foreign Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and relevant specialized committees, responsible for supervising the work of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, including the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's work in sustainability, and submitting recommendations. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, is responsible for leading the overall Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategies and policies of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority at the management level. In terms of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office is responsible for coordinating and supervising ESG-related work within the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office. Furthermore, regarding other functional areas, the relevant groups and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures related to the development of banks and the market to the operations of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority itself. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group, jointly initiated and established by The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the work of various financial regulatory bodies, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion of the scope of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainability work over the past few years, we have therefore established a Steering Committee in October to serve as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the different functional areas of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. To provide guidance for the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans related to ESG matters in the four functional areas of the banking industry, market development, foreign exchange fund investment, and internal operations. Supervising the implementation of ESG-related plans by the various functional departments of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority. assess the performance and effectiveness of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority in achieving its ESG goals. and supervise external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with three deputy governors serving as permanent members. Additionally, we will invite the executive assistants responsible for key functions related to green and sustainability matters to attend the Steering Committee meeting to report on the main achievements of their work and future plans. The Steering Committee regularly convenes meetings, and relevant working groups under the purview of the banks division, institutional expansion and operations department, foreign affairs department, and the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority provide support. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) jointly established a supervisory group in May 2020. The steering group, as an inter-institutional platform, provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral work on how the financial industry should address climate and environmental risks, in order to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading global centre for green and sustainable finance in Asia and globally. For details regarding the work of the steering group, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the green and sustainable finance ecosystem."

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always been committed to consolidating the Hong Kong financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations. To continue to play its important function in the financial system and guide more capital towards green and sustainability projects, banks must proactively manage climate risk. As a banking regulatory body, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is particularly focused on building the capacity for banks to address climate risk and manage climate risk, and accelerating the work of banks to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to formulating various policy measures to strengthen the capacity of the banks system to address climate risk. In August, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority issued a net-zero transition plan announcement, outlining high-level principles to assist banks in maintaining safety and stability during the economic transition to net-zero emissions. After issuing the notice, we conducted a survey of some banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transformation plans. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices regarding transformation planning with the industry and will host seminars or workshops to facilitate industry exchange of experiences. Regarding disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments, including the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards published in June, and the consultation framework on the third pillar disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks launched by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in November, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is strengthening its work to improve the sustainability-related disclosure framework for banks in Hong Kong. Specifically, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is collaborating with local authorities and stakeholders in Hong Kong to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that complies with the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority strengthened supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided advice to banks to help them further enhance their climate response and climate risk management capabilities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the regulatory procedures of banks. Climate risk management is now listed as a standing agenda item for prudential supervisory meetings held by bank management. Banking supervisors also adopt the enhanced CAMEL rating system, which has already incorporated climate risk factors, to assess the risk status and risk management system of the banks. As part of implementing the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into banking supervision procedures, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has revised the green assessment framework to focus on the banks' transformation planning measures. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is also reviewing the supervisory review procedures for assessing and monitoring the capital adequacy levels of banks and determining their second pillar capital requirements, to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address climate risk. Following the completion of the 12-month implementation period for the "climate risk management" section GS-1 of the "Regulatory Policy Handbook" under the two-year plan in 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched a special review of climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. This thematic review covers four main areas, including the governance framework for climate-related risks, the oversight of climate strategies, the oversight of climate-related risk management, and organizational culture, awareness, and communication. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has made several improvements to its climate risk stress testing framework, including the introduction of new 5-year scenarios to assess the potential impact on banks from the simultaneous occurrence of economic and Climate change shocks. As part of the stress testing programme led by the regulatory authority conducted periodically by The Hong Kong Monetary Authority following improvements, the second round of climate risk stress testing commenced in June to comprehensively assess banks' climate risk exposures and further enhance banks' ability to manage climate risk. This is a risk stress test, involving 44 banks, an increase of over sixty percent compared to the initial testing plan in 2021. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also held a climate risk stress testing forum in November, with more than 300 bank employees participating. By promoting the sharing of experiences among banks, this activity helps deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review the progress of banks' implementation of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Regulatory Policy Handbook" Unit GS-1 "climate risk management." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and bank management held a meeting to discuss their work in climate risk management and the common challenges faced in the industry, and to review the information and other public disclosures provided by the banks to assess their progress. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority provides targeted advice to banks, encouraging and supporting banks to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in line with the Monetary Authority's regulatory expectations. As global attention to Climate change increases and efforts are made to address related issues, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has noted the growing demand for green and sustainability investment products, and some banks are also providing relevant products to meet client needs. In view of this, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has completed a special review of banks' sales of green and sustainability investment products and issued a notice in November, outlining the standards The Hong Kong Monetary Authority expects banks to meet and sharing observations of good practices. This announcement covers multiple areas including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and control, staff training, and bookkeeping records, aiming to reduce potential greenwashing risks and strengthen investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of related investment activities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainability in the banking sector. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, strengthening the ability of banks to manage climate risk. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is about to launch a cloud platform trial version to allow banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to cooperate with other central banks and regulatory bodies to explore how technological solutions can assist in the assessment of physical risks. On the other hand, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices through the application of advanced analytics and outlook, to reduce the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the data collection process for financial crime risk information, thereby strengthening the operational procedures for banks to submit anti-money laundering (AML) related information in a sustainable manner. In September, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority organized the "Green Fintech Competition" to seek solutions for market use to help the banking industry address the challenges of the following aspects: (i) net-zero transition or transformation planning. (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainability finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 submission proposals from approximately 70 companies. In December, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority organized the "Green and Sustainability Banking Seminar," providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the role of low-carbon technology and green fintech in Hong Kong and mainland China's net-zero transition, and simultaneously announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition." This activity attracted approximately 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulatory bodies, and academia. To enhance transparency in the financial markets and bring green and sustainability financial decisions into closer alignment, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with the assistance of consulting firms, has formulated a local green classified framework. In May, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority published a discussion paper on the "Hong Kong green classified framework prototype," soliciting shareholder opinions on the establishment and implementation of the green classified directory. Based on the consultation results, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is fine-tuning the framework prototype and identifying other aspects for the next phase of framework development. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority participates in the work of special organizations for financial action. The organization has confirmed the upstream offenses of money laundering related to environmental crimes, and due to the interconnectedness between anti-money laundering (AML) and environmental, social, and governance (ESG), this scope is increasingly attracting attention from regulatory bodies. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is well aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; therefore, broader climate factors and scenarios should be incorporated into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current supervisory work. In the process of continuously monitoring financial stability risks, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will consider climate change and include an analysis of climate-related risks in all financial stability reports. Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis working group under the "central and regulatory bodies green finance network" (NGFS), The Hong Kong Monetary Authority assists in further enriching climate scenarios, enabling the central and regulatory bodies to gain a clearer understanding of the impact of Climate change on the macroeconomy and finance. As a member of the working group for transformation planning under the Financial Stability Board, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority participates in analyzing the interplay between the transformation planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to form a forward-looking and dynamic perspective for reviewing climate-related finance risks. In terms of research work, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority conducts multiple applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the finance industry and the economy. The research topics include the climate risk bearing of the banking and investment fund sectors, the flow of ESG funds, the impact of Climate change on property prices, and the ripple effect of corporate ESG in the global supply chain. The research findings above enhance The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's understanding of the impact of Climate change and ESG issues on finance stability, which aids in formulating relevant policies. Locally, these studies help strengthen The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's continuous monitoring and assess of the impact of climate risk on finance stability. Externally, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also shares research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels, including international activities on climate-related issues and the "The Hong Kong Monetary Authority Research Memorandum." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Liquidity Funding Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized reserve funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework, as recommended by the NGFS. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and promoting sustainability in finance as the mainstream. Through participation in this area, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority helps promote policy dialogue internationally and regionally on addressing Climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws insights from this to enhance the climate response capacity of the Hong Kong financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as the region's leading green and sustainable finance hub, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has worked closely with local and international partners to co-build a richer ecosystem and promote the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group shall be jointly led by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission, responsible for coordinating the financial industry's response measures to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the government's climate strategy. The supervisory team has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the supervisory team announced the main measures to support Hong Kong in seizing the opportunities of sustainable finance, the main areas of work of which include sustainable disclosure, strengthening the ecosystem, financial transition, and green finance technology. Specifically, the Sustainability Disclosure Working Group has been established to formulate the roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of IFRS sustainability disclosure standards. This roadmap will include four key areas, including sustainable reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. Additionally, a transformation finance working group has been established to explore methods for supporting financial institutions and enterprises in planning and reporting on transformation. The supervisory team also strengthens the construction of a sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. Especially in terms of data, we continue to promote the adoption of the supervisory team for the non-public company climate and environmental risk questionnaire 2 launched in 2022 in cooperation with CDP. The supervisory team will continue to closely follow the latest developments in the green and sustainable finance sector and enhance Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region and globally. In January 2024, the supervisory team announced three new key initiatives to seize the investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To provide skills training beneficial to the industry, the green and sustainable finance center under the supervision of the supervisory team will implement the government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Program," providing subsidies to employees, students, and graduates who receive training related to green and sustainable finance and obtain relevant qualifications. In December 2023, there were a total of 46 international and local training or qualifications registered as eligible training or qualifications under this program, and over 560 grant applications were approved. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also launched a foundational level new module for "green and sustainable finance" under the "banking professional qualifications framework" for banks. This module aims to promote talent development in the banking industry and enhance the overall professional capabilities of employees. In 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to collaborate with the banking industry to develop the professional level of this unit to meet the industry's rapidly growing demand for professionals in green and sustainable finance. To help financial institutions and enterprises, especially SMEs, better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainable reporting, greenhouse gas emission calculations, and planning on transformation, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and relevant government decision-making bureaus and departments, as well as global partners such as the CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ)3, and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financial (PCAF)4, will jointly organize a series of seminars and workshops during the year to attract participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. Regarding students, following the launch of the "sustainable finance internship program" in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to deepen the understanding of sustainable finance for interns and undergraduate degree graduates. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority recognizes the potential of DeepMind Technology in filling data gaps related to climate and improving data quality, and is therefore committed to making the relevant data more accessible for viewing and use, and to enhancing data quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the supervisory team launched a series of website optimization measures to provide a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information for financial institutions, enterprises, and the public. Key optimization items include a sustainable disclosure electronic platform, greenhouse gas emission calculations and estimation tools, as well as more centralized, browsable, and searchable data and resources. During the "Hong Kong Green Week," the supervisory team also co-organized the "Leveraging Technology to Catalyze Sustainable Finance" activities with the Digital Hong Kong and Investment Promotion Agency to showcase leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's advantages in green technology. The "Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Theme" was held from February 26 to March 1, 2024, during which various activities themed on sustainable development attracted over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 regions, including representatives from financial institutions, enterprises, central banks, international organizations, government agencies, academia, and consulting firms. The focal activities of "Hong Kong Green Week" are the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum," co-organized by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and international financial companies. The forum gathered over 400 guests, including top decision-makers in the global business and finance sectors, to discuss solutions for climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. This is a broad set of topics for the two-day activities, including energy transition, decarbonization of heavy industry, circular economy, the future development of sustainable finance, and new climate technologies in emerging and developing markets of the Asia-Pacific region. The forum has received responses from public and private organizations, co-hosting over 10 round tables, seminars, and other exchange activities. The topics cover climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance classified, and green development financing in the Belt and Road Initiative regions. In addition, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the International Monetary Fund co-hosted the "Asia Climate Finance Round Tables" on February 29, 2024, to discuss key measures for expanding the scale of climate finance, as well as the role of central banks and regulatory bodies in climate risk management. The aforementioned activities are part of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's overall work to promote and enrich the green and sustainable finance ecosystem in Hong Kong, and can serve as a useful platform to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address the challenges of climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always actively supported the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, international financial companies and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched the "Green Commercial Bank Alliance" to jointly develop a cooperation platform for green commercial banks, gathering financial institutions, the banking industry, research institutions, and innovative technology providers within the region. Since March 2021, the alliance has held 22 training activities and round tables, attracting over 7,300 participants from various global locations including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. The alliance, in October, published a second topical research report titled "Developing Progressive Green Banking Industry Climate Strategies: A Case Study" in collaboration with Crédit Agricole CIB. The alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB jointly published the topical research report "Developing Progressive Green Banking Industry Climate Strategies: A Case Study" in October. During the year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office joined the newly established "Sustainable Investment Capability Building Alliance" (CASI) and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the international "Belt and Road Initiative" green development alliance. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and guide more funding towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and broader regions. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of a Hong Kong branch to support the net-zero emission work of financial institutions in Hong Kong and mainland China. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority assists GFANZ in a consultative role. To demonstrate the government's response to climate change, and its commitment to promoting green finance and striving to develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable development and livable city, the government launched the "Government Green Bond Program" in 2018. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority assists in the issuance of green bonds under the program. The government has to date issued approximately 25 billion dollar equivalent green institutional and retail bonds, with the proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recycling, energy efficiency, and energy saving. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the program, The government annually publishes the "green bonds report," detailing the allocation of funds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. The government continued its regular issuance of green institutional bonds in the 2023 to 2024 fiscal year, and issued approximately 6 billion dollar equivalent green bonds in June. This is a series of bonds of different maturities denominated in the dollar, euro, and renminbi, attracting investors of various categories, with enthusiastic subscription, recording subscription amounts equivalent to nearly 30 billion dollars. The issuance amount of renminbi bonds increased from 10 billion renminbi issued in January to 15 billion renminbi, and a 10-year renminbi bond was introduced for the first time, which will help extend the government's renminbi yield curve and further enrich the selection of offshore renminbi products. Global investors have reacted enthusiastically to the government's issuance of green bonds, reflecting investors' affirmation of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, The government issued the second tranche of HK$20 billion in green retail bonds, further promoting market development and advancing inclusive finance. This issuance provides citizens with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, allowing them to participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

The Monetary Authority plays a key role in promoting green and sustainable finance development to support the global climate agenda as an important global asset holder and manager. The Monetary Authority has always been a pioneer of responsible investment. Since 2015, The Monetary Authority has been leading green and sustainable asset investment, requiring external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights and to integrate environmental, social, and governance factors into the investment management of foreign exchange funds. The Monetary Authority invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "preserve principal first, long-term appreciation," believing that thorough consideration of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors helps to reduce related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of the investment. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a "2050 net-zero emissions" target for its "investment portfolio" 2, The Monetary Authority is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasizing sustainability, especially the urgent issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of foreign exchange funds and pursue more desirable risk-adjusted long-term returns. As responsible investors, The Monetary Authority participates in building a robust green and sustainable financial ecosystem, collaborating with investors, regulatory bodies, and international organizations with similar philosophies to establish industry operational standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment by the financial industry and central banks. Through supervisory and cooperative measures, The Monetary Authority is committed to promoting a future where finance and sustainable development run in parallel. Figure 1: Comprehensive and reliable ESG information for foreign exchange funds' responsible investment journey is crucial for integrating sustainability and planning credible climate transition to achieve net-zero goals. To fulfill its commitment to support the central and regulatory bodies' green finance network (NGFS) and the Glasgow Declaration, as well as the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Sectoral Steering Group's strategy plan, The Monetary Authority is implementing, in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), this chapter on responsible investment for foreign exchange funds. The Foreign Exchange Funds Advisory Committee, chaired by the Director of the Ministry of Finance, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented in the investment management of the foreign exchange funds by the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. The primary guiding principles establish the tone for The Monetary Authority to practice responsible investment while also considering the investment objectives of foreign exchange funds. The Investment Committee under the purview of the Foreign Exchange Funds Advisory Committee is chaired by the Governor of The Monetary Authority and is responsible for supervising the ESG and climate-related risks associated with foreign exchange funds investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policy, and monitors the implementation status through the regular meeting reports of the sustainable investment subcommittee of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office is chaired by the Chief Strategist and is responsible for coordinating and supervising all ESG work of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. The motions and progress of work discussed by the ESG Committee at the quarterly meeting will be reported to the President of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. Furthermore, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee, chaired by the Governor of The Monetary Authority, the CEO of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, and the Chief Strategist, convenes semi-annually to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures of various functions within The Monetary Authority, including the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, to implement The Monetary Authority's overall ESG objectives. Figure 2 shows the responsible investment governance framework of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office as shown in Figure 1. The Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office commenced its responsible investment journey in 2016, with the initial focus being on managing ESG risks that may affect the financial performance of the foreign exchange funds. As sustainable development rapidly evolves and surpasses risk considerations to become a priority strategic focus for major institutions globally, the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office has re-examined its responsible investment approach. July 2023 marked another milestone, with the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office establishing a new business strategy division led by the Chief Strategist, responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, and incorporating the responsible investment task force, formerly under the Risk Management and Supervision Department, which is now called the sustainable investment subcommittee. This strategic adjustment reflects The Monetary Authority's shift in investment focus from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing investment matters related to sustainable development. The sustainable investment subcommittee and the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office collaborate closely in integrating ESG factors, assisting the senior personnel of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office in managing the ESG risks and opportunities, especially climate-related ones, for various investment projects: Public market investments—the situation where credit, regulatory, and supervisory committees composed of senior personnel from the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office review ESG factors after incorporating the opinions of the sustainable investment subcommittee into credit risk models, and the ESG status of fixed-income portfolios is monitored through regular reports from the Risk Management and Supervision Department. Furthermore, the sustainable investment subcommittee also participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring process of external investment managers for stock portfolios from an ESG perspective (see the section "Promoting the active exercise of ownership" in the "Risk Management" section on page 40). Private Market Investment— —The Investment Committee, chaired by the Governor of The Monetary Authority, will consider the ESG-related assess made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment recommendation. The Monetary Authority understands that the physical and transition risks associated with climate change, as well as related opportunities, will affect the long-term performance and value of foreign exchange funds investment projects. The United Nations Environment Programme's "2023 Emissions Gap Report" projects that unless greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced globally, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more progressive policies, technological development, or behavioral changes to control rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks such as asset devaluation or asset lock-in. At the same time, extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and increasingly severe, also posing additional physical risks to investment projects. The Monetary Authority believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of foreign exchange funds, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. The Monetary Authority set the goal for the "investment portfolio" of the foreign exchange funds to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier in 2022, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The Monetary Authority continues to strengthen its work across the three pillars and clearly focuses on decarbonization and transformation. The following sections will detail the relevant methods. Figure 3 illustrates that in pursuing net-zero goals through responsible investment, The Monetary Authority tends to proactively engage in communication and avoid excluding or withdrawing from its investment projects. First, maintaining a diversified and stable asset portfolio plays a key role in achieving the primary investment objective of foreign exchange funds. Directly excluding certain categories or industries will narrow the investment universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risk. Through compatible approaches, The Monetary Authority can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transformation, possessing excellent technology and good corporate governance to respond to changing global climate trends, including companies belonging to high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires a core "brown" industries transformation. Only exclude relevant investment projects or withdraw investment to help solve carbon emission problems. Conversely, The Monetary Authority supports these industries in implementing a transformation to sustainable and low-carbon operating methods by investing strategic capital and actively exercising ownership rights, thereby bringing about beneficial changes for themselves and for the global. In response to market development, The Monetary Authority is refining its net-zero investment strategy, employing comprehensive methods to pursue transformation outcomes that align with foreign exchange funds and global net-zero goals, while adhering to its guiding principles of responsible investment. The Monetary Authority continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities by integrating ESG factors into investment decisions to promote the climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the foreign exchange funds' asset portfolio (Figure 4). The Monetary Authority's responsible investment maintained a good momentum in 2023. In the public market, The Monetary Authority is launching a new active global equity investment portfolio with a theme of sustainability and climate transition, managed by external investment managers, and will expand the application of customized low-carbon stock indices to another asset portfolio managed by external investment managers. Furthermore, The Monetary Authority prioritizes the performance of green, social responsibility, and sustainable development bonds for investment, demonstrating the philosophy of "doing good and getting rich." In the private market sector, The Monetary Authority is actively building robust long-term growth portfolios, seizing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic development trends such as climate and energy transition. For example, the Monetary Authority invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds during the year, demonstrating the Monetary Authority's responsibility for addressing the needs of the Asia climate transition. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) is committed to becoming a sustainable institution, implementing multiple measures to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) also emphasizes employee physical and mental health and social responsibility, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. As a responsible institution, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) sets sustainable development goals under the three pillars of environmental, employee, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), established in October, is chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) and is the principal decision-making body for various institutional sustainability measures. The Steering Committee was the predecessor of the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for leading the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) in formulating the vision, strategies, and policies for corporate sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Assistant President (Institutional Development and Operations) supervises the execution of sustainable development activities and submits progress reports to the Steering Committee regularly. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Group provide support for the organizing body's sustainability work. The former serves as a platform for discussing how to create a green working environment through brainstorming, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) has formulated a roadmap to guide its transformation direction. The focus is on implementing carbon reduction strategies in daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centers, practicing green commuting, adopting energy-saving measures, utilizing digital tools and more environmentally friendly operating models, waste reduction, and establishing a culture of sustainable development. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) also plans to utilize carbon embedding tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and for emissions that are difficult to reduce, it will adopt carbon offsetting measures. In addition to the environmental commitments related to its daily operations mentioned above, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) continues to introduce more environmentally friendly operational plans for the broader society, covering channels applicable to banks for submitting electronic documents and communications, as well as electronic payment and coin collection schemes for public use. To strengthen and maintain its operational capacity, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) has hired a professional working team, established a talent pool, and emphasizes employee physical and mental well-being. In terms of social responsibility, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities. In procurement, consider selecting social enterprises. Promote financial services consumer education, and cooperate with the banking industry to ensure that all sectors of society can equitably access basic banking services and consumption. The remainder of this chapter details the specifics of the aforementioned strategies. Under the overall institutional risk management framework of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank), the Risk Committee, chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank), considers the potential risks and threats that The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) faces in its daily operations, including potential risks and threats caused by climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as more extreme weather causing flooding or other damage, may affect The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s offices and impede employee travel. To manage entity risk, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) regularly updates its ongoing operation plans to respond to extreme weather situations. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility drills to ensure employees are always prepared to implement continuity of operations measures. The office design also incorporates multiple measures to mitigate potential risks. Transformation risk may affect The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s energy consumption, air travel, and waste disposal. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) continuously monitors the transformation risks it faces by tracking its greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s climate goal is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) by 2050 or sooner across all operational scopes of the organization. As a recent emission reduction target, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing vehicles to electric vehicles. Using 2015 as the base year, through various carbon reduction and offsetting strategies, reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier. Despite challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) will take a multi-pronged approach within feasible scope to minimize greenhouse gas emissions in Scope 3 (such as paper usage, waste generation, and air travel, etc.). The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets are formulated by reference to the "Science-Based Targets Initiative" methodology, a methodology that has also been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) has commissioned the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emission, energy consumption, paper usage, and waste data disclosed in this report. The scope and criteria for verification are stated in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank), in addition to publishing the 2022 Annual Report, also independently published the 2022 Sustainability Report for the first time. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's efforts to strengthen ESG reporting have been recognized, receiving an ESG award in the "Public Sector" category at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Award 2023." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) is the first financial regulatory institution to receive this category award. The review panel praises the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) for achieving good ESG standards; the Sustainability Report is clear and easy to read, and the appointment of an independent body to verify its goal-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflects its commitment to high transparency and accountability in reporting. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) also received the highest rating in the "Non-profit and Charitable Organization" category gold award in the Hong Kong Professional Association's "2023 Best Annual Report Award" selection. The review panel commended the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial data and for effectively utilizing infographics, demonstrating the Monetary Authority's commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. In recognition of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s commitment to the environment, employees, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Social Services Association has continuously awarded the "15 Years + United in Care" emblem to The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) is committed to properly managing the environmental impact of its operations, and its internal "Green Office Guidelines" provide employees with guidance on resource utilization and the generation of office waste. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) has integrated environmental factors into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When renovating the office, reuse existing furniture and finishing materials as much as possible to reduce waste, and prioritize the use of environmentally friendly building and decorative materials. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has consistently followed this practice, and in 2021 and 2022, the office for the portion of its second phase renovation at the international financial center was awarded LEED 7 and the "Green Building Environmental Assessment" 8 certification. Through the adoption of new technologies and the effective utilization of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency, it remains one of the key focuses of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank). In addition to promoting good habits, such as turning off unnecessary lighting devices within the work area outside of working hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include using fluorescent tube lighting equipment, activity sensors, setting the air conditioning room temperature to an appropriate level, and utilizing energy in the information technology network infrastructure. The energy consumption of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) continues to decrease, reaching 2.59 TWh per person in 2023, a decrease of 29.7% from the 2015 criteria (Figure 1). Based on the nature of the daily operations of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank), its greenhouse gas emissions primarily originate from greenhouse gas emissions caused by the electricity consumed, which is generated by fossil fuels. In 2023, the total emission intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuels and electricity was 1.48 tCO e10 per person, a decrease of 45.2% compared to 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardized equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) also adopts digital tools and technology, automates and streamlines work processes, and builds a digital work environment to enhance online collaboration within the offices. The paperless meeting has become the main meeting method of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank). To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, all internal administrative affairs primarily utilize electronic processes. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) encourages employees to integrate into green and digitalized work models, replacing paper documents and communication with digital methods. The implementation of the electronic record backup system is also in progress. The aforementioned green and digitalized measures bring positive results. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's paper density in 2023 was 11.55 kilograms per person, a significant decrease of 64.8% compared to 2015 (Figure 3). Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, most international activities have returned to in-person formats, and simultaneously, the development of Hong Kong's position as an international financial center must be promoted; therefore, relevant staff of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) inevitably need to travel overseas for official duties. To reduce carbon emissions caused by air travel, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) encourages employees to take direct flights or combine different official travel itineraries where feasible when participating in overseas activities. At the institutional level, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) participates in the "Gold Standard" 12 certified carbon offset program to offset the remaining carbon emissions caused by air travel. This project involves waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s procurement process should consider sustainability and environmental factors. As part of the comprehensive review of procurement policies and procedures for the organization, the current practice of procuring green products has been established as a formal system and complies with the environmental standards of the government's "Green Procurement Checklist," particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office supplies. Furthermore, the tender assessment criteria have also included ESG factors and innovative suggestions that can enhance productivity and efficiency. Furthermore, all suppliers must commit to complying with environmental regulations. In accordance with the "4R" principles, namely Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) adopts a three-pronged approach to minimize waste generation and manage the disposal of waste. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to assist in formulating targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste transported to the landfill and various recyclable wastes, are contained in the "Summary of Performance" section on page 56. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) first directly participated in the gift recovery program for the management company of the International Financial Center office building in 2023. Employees collectively submitted approximately 3,000 used but still in good condition letters. These letters will be handed over to an environmental organization for distribution to the public for use in the Lunar New Year next year. Given that the operation of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) and the backup data centers constitute the main portion of the organization's overall energy consumption, two data centers have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by green building environmental assessments for existing data centers, achieving optimal energy usage efficiency (Power Usage Effectiveness, abbreviated as PUE) 13. In 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's two data centers received "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings, respectively, based on the assessment guidelines "Green Building Environmental Assessment for Existing Data Centers" issued in 2021. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) is the first and only institution in Hong Kong to have received such a rating. Improving the energy efficiency of the two data centers has always been a focus of the technical team. For this, the team adopted green design in the renovation project and employed good operational practices that are energy-efficient to reduce PUE and achieve relevant targets, including 24-hour monitoring of the data centers' environmental facilities and continuous improvement of environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. As the technical team continuously improves the energy utilization of data centers, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) appointed an external consultant in December 2021 to review and comprehensively assess the green level of the data centers, and to formulate recommendations to further enhance performance in all aspects. The research was completed in 2022. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) also began preparations for certification eligibility for "green data centers" under the "green building environmental assessment" certification program shortly after the research was completed. The certification process is very comprehensive and rigorous. During the full year of 2023, the technical team implemented optimization measures based on the recommendations of the consultant report to improve energy performance and the health elements of the working environment within the data centers.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency independently verified the 2023 environmental data ("2023 data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2023 data includes the total energy consumption for 2023, greenhouse gas emissions for scope 1 and scope 2, business aviation travel greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, generated non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), their respective densities, and the changes compared to the 2015 levels. Furthermore, the 2023 data also includes the amount of kitchen waste generated during that year, its intensity, and the change compared to the level when the kitchen waste recycling scheme was launched by the HKMA in November 2022. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emission data is compiled according to the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol) system, developed jointly by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council of Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covers data from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2023, and also includes relevant data used for comparison of annual performance during the period from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2015 (excluding food waste). The scope of verification covers five office and warehouse assets, of which four offices are located in 1) International Finance Centre Phase II, 2) HSBC Centre, 3) Takashimaya Square Phase I, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, while the warehouse is in 5) Lokesung Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of this verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and support evidence from five selected assets. This verification work is conducted in accordance with the "International Verification Engagement Guidelines 3000 (Revised Edition)" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provision for "Verification engagements other than the audit or review of historical financial data." The verification procedure is designed to make opinions and summaries to obtain a reasonable degree of assurance. The verification process is determined according to the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The validation process involved tracing the selected sample data back to its source to test the integrity and accuracy of the data, as well as reviewing the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducting reliability testing.
