The verification process also includes verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, visiting representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 data, and selecting representative data and information for auditing. The relevant original data and support evidence have also undergone detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency's verification team did not participate in the 2023 data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reasonably assures and summarizes that the 2023 data is substantially accurate and reliable. The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is sufficient. Shen Xiaoyin Review Supervisor The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making accelerated global climate action imperative. The World Meteorological Organization confirms that 2024 was the hottest year on record, and the first year in which global temperatures exceeded pre-industrial levels by a critical 1.5 degrees Celsius. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions have eased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached a new high, highlighting the inadequacy of current measures to mitigate climate change. In addressing global warming, the manifestation of climate-related risks will intensify, and the impact on economic and financial markets is difficult to predict. Furthermore, with the current geopolitical situation tense, the global economic landscape is becoming increasingly fragmented, energy security issues are feared to escalate, and with an uncertain economic outlook, all pose greater challenges for countries in addressing climate change. The process of low-carbon economic transition requires substantial and continuous financial support. In the global, the transformation challenges faced, especially in Asia, are the most severe. As pointed out by the World Economic Forum, Asia is not only an engine of global economic growth but also the region most susceptible to the impacts of climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a key role in whether the global goal of achieving net-zero emissions can be successfully reached. As a leading international financial center in Asia, Hong Kong needs to strengthen its leading role and fully utilize the power of finance to support and drive transformation in the region. Therefore, the Monetary Authority published the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" last year, outlining our vision and roadmap for gradually integrating sustainable development concepts into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on strengthening the financial industry's capacity to address risks related to climate change, and on the other hand, focuses on assisting the industry in grasping related new opportunities. Furthermore, we set an example and play a leading role. The Monetary Authority's sustainable development work includes four areas: support for the banking sector to move towards net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and advancing more inclusive sustainable development. The banks' system plays a key role in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and Asia, but they also face numerous risks during the transition process. In the "Action Plan," we have set ambitious goals, requiring all banks to commit to achieving net-zero emissions in their operations by 2030 or earlier, and achieving net-zero emissions in financing by 2050 or earlier. We also require all banks to enhance the disclosure of risks and opportunities related to climate change. While continuously strengthening the management of bank climate risks, we also provide guidance for banks' transformation planning, assisting them to enhance their capacity to respond to transformation and better manage related risks. We are also currently undertaking preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, striving to further enhance industry transparency in these activities. Furthermore, we are optimizing the Hong Kong sustainable finance classified directory launched in May of last year to include more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We expect to guide more capital towards sustainable and transformative projects by providing clear guidelines. Climate change brings significant entity and transformative risks, which may affect the long-term financial performance and value of foreign exchange fund investment projects. At the same time, it also brings opportunities for growth and a positive impact to the foreign exchange fund. Our experience proves that investment returns and positive sustainable impacts can be mutually aligned, without conflict. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the "investment portfolio" of the foreign exchange fund by 2050 or earlier, and in the "Action Plan," we pledge to support Asia's transformative climate transform through the investment of the foreign exchange fund. Currently, the proportion of sustainable investment in the investment portfolio has exceeded ten percent. To further promote sustainable investment within the region, the Monetary Authority established a strategic partnership with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and international financial institutions in November of last year to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in the Asia region through joint investment. Furthermore, we published the first "Monetary Authority ESG Expectations" document in September of last year to further encourage fund managers to proactively exercise ownership rights and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Financial communication is particularly important for accelerating the transformative within the region. As an international financial hub, and as the preferred location for issuers within Asia (including provincial and municipal governments in mainland China) to issue international sustainable bonds, Hong Kong plays a crucial role in guiding capital to accelerate transformative change within the region. The Action Plan outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable development financing platform, and the goals of promoting sustainable financial innovation within the region. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to drive green bond innovation (including the issuance of the first batch of multi-currency digital bonds globally in February last year), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Support Scheme" to transformative financing instruments in May last year, to the launch of the "Digital Bond Support Scheme" in November last year, we have consistently strived to encourage issuers within the region to utilize Hong Kong's financial platforms to raise the necessary funds for carbon reduction and transformation. To achieve a robust transformative, in addition to capital and innovation, a inclusive and participatory sustainable development system is needed for support. This includes reliable sustainable development data, high-transparency information disclosure, and industry talent with relevant knowledge and skills. Here, in the "Action Plan," we commit to supporting the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, and to striving to fill the gap in sustainable finance talent and knowledge within the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, particularly by providing user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainable disclosure for small and medium-sized enterprises. We also launched the professional-level module "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the banks professional qualifications framework last November to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local bank employees. Furthermore, through the first Hong Kong Green Week and other activities held in February of last year, we allowed various sectors to participate in discussions on sustainable development, thereby promoting cooperation and innovation. Within the Monetary Authority, we are committed to ensuring operations align with the vision of sustainable development. In our Action Plan, we commit to achieving net-zero emissions in our operations by 2030 or sooner, which is 20 years ahead of our original commitment. Furthermore, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap issued by the government. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low carbon emissions as a screening factor in the procurement process. Simultaneously, we continue to improve work efficiency through digitalization and cultivate a culture of sustainable development within the organization, encouraging employees to actively participate in sustainable development initiatives. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic changes in the geopolitical situation have added variables to global climate action. However, climate change is an undeniable fact and is gradually intensifying. In addressing climate change, the current situation does not permit us to be in the slightest slack. We firmly believe that promoting an orderly and inclusive transformative process will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on the Hong Kong financial system and bring opportunities for us in the process. Entering 2025, we will continue to strive forward, endeavor to promote sustainable development work, and deepen relationships with partners who share similar philosophies. Despite facing severe challenges, we will continue to be committed to supporting the construction of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia, and other regions.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the current generation. As an international financial center and a sustainable finance hub in the Asia region, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development from Asia to the global. The People's Bank of China announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan") in October 2024, outlining the People's Bank of China's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timelines for achieving the targets of each initiative, and how we expect the industry to collaborate in promoting related work. The People's Bank of China plans to consolidate the financial industry in Hong Kong and the People's Bank of China's own capacity to address Climate change risks through the formulation of strategic policies, strengthening regulatory links, and improving internal operations, and to promote the transformation of the Asia region towards a more sustainable economy. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, The People's Bank of China is also committed to exerting influence in formulating green and sustainable finance policies and standards at regional and global levels. As a banking regulatory body, The People's Bank of China focuses on enhancing the climate change response capabilities of the banking sector and supporting banks in maintaining safety and stability during their transition to net-zero emissions. Our primary work for 2025 includes: - Launching a new round of thematic reviews on the climate risk management practices of banks and conducting a third round of consultation meetings to examine the situation of banks in implementing the relevant regulatory requirements of The People's Bank of China and to further strengthen the climate risk management capabilities of banks. To improve the work of the supervisory authority-led stress testing framework by incorporating climate risk stress testing into the supervision framework of the People's Bank of China. Continue to promote the work of incorporating climate factors into the supervisory review procedures of the People's Bank of China. Preparatory work is underway for the development of relevant regulatory requirements by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision for the third pillar disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks and the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards, to be implemented in the domestic banking sector. Completed the compilation of the new module GS-2 of the "Regulatory Policy Manual" to provide guidance for the transformation planning for banks. And - share best practices regarding climate risk management and the application of green financial technology with the industry. In addition to its role as a regulator of the banking sector, The People's Bank of China also plays a promotional role, striving to promote the development of a green and sustainable financial ecosystem and to support banks in providing financing for transformation. We have published the first phase of the "Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classified Catalogue," providing the industry with tools to identify green and sustainable economic activities, and to promote related financial flows. The People's Bank of China has launched the second phase of work on the classified catalog to expand the scope of coverage, including incorporating transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate change adaptation goals. Furthermore, building upon the success of the third FiNETech activities in 2024 and the green financial technology competition in 2023, we will host another green financial technology activity for 2025 to promote the adoption of green financial technology solutions by banks. Hong Kong possesses superior conditions to support sustainable financing needs within the area. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the government in promoting the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme," which has expanded its scope to include sustainable projects, such as social responsibility initiatives. This move will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a model for other potential issuers in the region. Furthermore, we will continue to provide funding through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Support Scheme," encouraging more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable funds. We will also strengthen promotional efforts to encourage more government, institutional, and corporate entities from Mainland China and other regions to raise green finance in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will also continue to catalyze and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing support to digital green bond issuers through the "Digital Bond Financing Program." Although the market demand for high-quality sustainable disclosures by institutions and corporations is increasing, the capabilities and preparedness of different entities in making sustainable disclosures vary, and some entities may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the People's Bank of China will continue to cooperate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance cross-institutional supervisory group to make sustainable disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with more comprehensive climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainable disclosures templates and supporting tools. Explore how to utilize technology to make existing resources more convenient and user-friendly. and cooperate with local major industry organizations to provide industry-required training. The sustainable finance market is volatile, requiring the expansion of the local talent pool and the filling of knowledge gaps from Hong Kong to in the region. The People's Bank of China's main work for 2025 includes cooperating with the banking sector to develop professional-level training courses for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework," as well as identifying areas where the industry has a need for further training through the forthcoming research on "Future Banking Sector Talent for 2026 to 2030." Furthermore, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to strengthen the promotion of the government-subsidized "Green and Sustainable Finance training pilot program" and review the scope of the program. At the regional level, The People's Bank of China will continue to collaborate with international financial institutions through the "Green Commercial Bank Alliance" to launch specialized programs in the Asia region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted skills enhancement and training support, promoting community engagement, facilitating access to potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in developing roadmaps to make green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, The People's Bank of China commits that the foreign exchange fund's "portfolio" will achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier to support the overall economic transition. We will continuously enhance the sustainability of foreign exchange fund investments through pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment methods, primarily focusing on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that promote positive climate outcomes. The People's Bank of China strives to set an example in the work of the sustainability of institutions. In response to the timeline for accelerating the achievement of net-zero commitments announced in the "Action Plan," The People's Bank of China will gradually incorporate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting in a pragmatic manner, continuing to promote the sustainable development of institutions. Specifically, we will conduct a dual materiality assessment for 2025 to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring we focus on material topics. Furthermore, we will conduct energy audits and assess the impact of climate risks on our offices and operations using technology solutions to enhance our climate change adaptation capacity and risk preparedness. We support the government's release of the "Hong Kong sustainable disclosures roadmaps" and are actively undertaking preparations to make disclosures in accordance with ISSB standards. In for 2025, The People's Bank of China will continue to uphold its commitment, selecting data centers for the planned upgrade projects based on energy efficiency and energy-saving principles. We will also expand digital measures to promote sustainable development and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and to improve the overall digital experience for our employees, banks, and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating these impacts. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and the wider Asia region through its multiple roles as a central bank institution, a regulator of the banking industry, a market facilitator, a responsible investor, and a sustainability institution. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has a sound sustainable development governance framework that leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Supervise the implementation of relevant measures. and ensure that the operations and working methods of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority incorporate sustainable development factors. To strive for good corporate governance, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has established a sound sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for related work. The governance framework ensures that the strategic planning and decision-making process of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority effectively integrates sustainability factors, and establishes effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and outcomes of sustainability work. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainability governance framework includes: - the Foreign Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and relevant specialized committees, responsible for supervising the work of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, including the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's work in sustainability, and submitting recommendations. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, is responsible for leading the overall Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategies and policies of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority at the management level. In terms of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office is responsible for coordinating and supervising ESG-related work within the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office. Furthermore, regarding other functional areas, the relevant committees and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures related to the development of banks and the market, as well as the operations of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority itself. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group, jointly initiated and established by The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the work of various financial regulatory bodies, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion of the scope of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainability work over the past several years, we therefore established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the different functional areas of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. To provide guidance for the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans related to ESG matters in the four functional areas of the banking industry, the green and sustainable finance ecosystem development, foreign exchange fund investment, and internal operations. Supervising the implementation of ESG-related plans by the various functional departments of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority. assess the performance and effectiveness of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority in achieving its ESG goals. and - supervise external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with three deputy governors serving as permanent members. Additionally, we will invite the executive assistants responsible for key functions related to green and sustainability matters to attend the Steering Committee meeting to report on the main achievements of their work and future plans. The Steering Committee regularly convenes meetings, and relevant working groups under the purview of the banks division, institutional expansion and operations department, foreign affairs department, and the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority provide support. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) jointly established a supervisory group in May 2020. The steering group, as an inter-institutional platform, provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral work on how the financial industry should address climate and environmental risks, in order to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading global centre for green and sustainable finance in Asia and globally. For details regarding the work of the steering group, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the green and sustainable finance ecosystem."

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always been committed to strengthening the capacity of the Hong Kong financial system to address climate risks, while also contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations, and therefore must proactively manage climate risks. Meanwhile, banks play an important role in the financial system, guiding funds towards green and sustainable projects. As a banking regulatory body, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is particularly focused on building the capacity for banks to address and manage climate risks, and accelerating the work of banks to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("the Action Plan"), outlining the Monetary Authority's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a sustainable finance hub in the region and to support sustainable development from Asia to the global level. The Action Plan includes eight major objectives across four aspects. To assist the industry in achieving the goals of the relevant banks' policies, we have consistently carried out the following tasks. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero financing by 2050 or earlier. In December, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the industry will share good practices for transition planning and conduct industry consultations on the draft of section GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the "Regulatory Policy Handbook." This new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing the capacity of banks to respond to the net-zero transition and related risk management. Furthermore, we are reviewing the supervisory review procedures for assessing and monitoring the adequacy of banks' capital levels and determining their second-pillar capital requirements, with the objective of incorporating factors proposed by the Basel Committee on effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risks. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always been committed to aligning local sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards and the Basel Committee's third pillar disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is analyzing the latest developments in sustainable disclosures and supports the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants to conduct a technical feasibility study on the adoption of ISSB standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the "the Action Plan". In May, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority published the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance classified directory to address industry concerns about greenwashing and to assist in guiding capital flows towards green and sustainable activities. The classified directory covers 12 economic activities across four industries, aiming to align with the common green classification directory and the classification directories of China and the EU, while also incorporating relevant elements to address local conditions. We have launched the second phase of work to expand the scope of the classified directory and are consulting with a broad range of stakeholders to further promote the flow of green and sustainable financing. During the year, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will further strengthen supervision of banks' climate risks risk management and is committed to support banks in building the capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and respond to Climate change. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has also completed all work to incorporate climate risks into the supervision procedures of banks in the two-year plan formulated in 2022. To promote the ability of banks to strengthen their management of climate risks, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority shares good practices observed in specialized review and consultation meetings within the banking sector, mainly including: - Establishing a robust governance framework, clearly defining the responsibilities of the board of directors and senior management - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas related to climate-related risks (1) Promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies (2) Take appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) establish a strong climate risks culture within the organization. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority held a roundtable meeting on climate risks risk management in August. At the round table meeting, representatives from the banks and participants from The Hong Kong Monetary Authority exchanged views on several climate risks-related issues, including the challenges banks face in climate risks risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. This round table meeting provided an interactive platform for information sharing and assisted The Hong Kong Monetary Authority in its work on climate risks and other related matters. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has launched a specialized review of the risk management frameworks and practices of banks concerning climate risks, and will assess their robustness and adequacy according to the regulatory expectations set out in Section GS-1 "Climate Risks Risk Management" of the "Regulatory Policy Handbook." The specialized review covers the entire risk management process, including risk identification, quantification, monitoring, reporting, control, and mitigation, as well as climate risks scenario analysis and stress testing. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority held the second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing Module GS-1 "climate risks risk management" of the "Regulatory Policy Handbook," and to understand the challenges they are facing. The consultation meetings also cover the latest regulations and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provide feedback and guidance based on the specific situation of the banks to support their climate risks risk management work. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority completed the second round of banking climate risk stress testing (CRST) in 2024, with 21 retail banks and 25 international bank group branches in Hong Kong participating. The results show that, under various scenarios (including the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and a macroeconomic downturn), the Hong Kong banking sector continues to demonstrate strong resilience in defending against severe climate-related shocks. Compared to the CRST pilot program, participating banks have significantly enhanced their capacity in measuring and assessing climate risks. The report detailing the CRST results and the good practices observed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority during the process was published in February 2025. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority understands the numerous data and methodological challenges that banks face in climate risks risk management, and therefore has been committed to various initiatives to promote the application of technology to address these challenges. To address the issue of lacking physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risks assess, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched a physical risk assessment platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will respond to user feedback and incorporate more local data to enhance the platform. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority collaborates with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green finance technology solutions by the banks and the overall finance services industry. During the year, we published practical application guides and two "Compliance Technology Use Case Presentations" (English version), explaining the technological solutions for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessment, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also hosted the third "FiNETech," gathering over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green finance technology cooperation. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is well aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; therefore, broader climate factors and scenarios should be incorporated into finance risk analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. In the process of continuously monitoring finance stability risks, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will take into account climate change and include analysis of climate-related risks in all finance stability reports. Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis working group under the "central and regulatory institution green finance network" (NGFS), The Hong Kong Monetary Authority assists in further enriching climate scenarios, helping the central and regulatory institutions understand the impact of Climate change on the macroeconomy and finance. In November, NGFS published the fifth edition of the long-term climate macro-finance scenarios to provide reference for forward-looking climate risks assessment. As a member of the transition planning working group under the Financial Stability Board, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority participates in analyzing the interplay between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to review climate-related finance risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has issued the "Practical Guidelines for the Application of Green Technology in Banks" (English version) to provide finance institutions with best practices for utilizing green technology to promote their net-zero transition. In terms of research work, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority conducts multiple applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change on the finance industry and the overall economy. The research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in resisting monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the finance industry in transitioning to a low-carbon economy. The aforementioned research findings not only enhance our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, assisting in the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies help strengthen The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's ongoing monitoring and assess the impact of Climate change on financial stability. The research findings are also shared with a broad base of stakeholders through various channels, including international forums and the "The Hong Kong Monetary Authority Research Memoranda." The Hong Kong Currency and Finance Research Centre (Research Centre), responsible for research work under the School of Finance, has published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. This study provides evidence indicating that low-emission corporate can gain significant benefits from carbon pricing, and highlights their role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission corporate. This research is published in the Research Centre's "Insights from Monetary Research" and is shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Liquidity Funding Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized reserve funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as the mainstream. Through participation in this area, we help promote policy dialogue between international and regional levels on addressing Climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draw insights from it to enhance the climate response capacity of the Hong Kong financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as the region's leading green and sustainable finance hub, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As outlined in the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to building Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers from the region to the global level, supporting technological innovation in the green areas of the financial market, enhancing industry sustainable disclosure, and expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing the knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. To build Hong Kong into the region's and global first-choice platform for sustainable finance, catalyzing support for sustainable finance innovation, and filling the talent and knowledge gaps in the region's sustainable finance through high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, to demonstrate the government's response to climate change and its commitment to promoting green finance and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable development and livable city, the government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. To date, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has assisted the government in jointly issuing green bonds equivalent to approximately 28 billion dollar, sold to institutional and retail investors. The raised funds are allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy saving. We seize every issuance opportunity, continuously innovating and expanding the characteristics of green bonds, including currency, maturity, and distribution channels, to lay the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the scheme and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scheme's scope was expanded to include sustainable projects, and it was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Scheme" (Sustainable Bond Scheme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Scheme, the government annually publishes the "green bonds report," detailing the allocation of funds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority assisted the government in July in issuing institutional green bonds worth approximately 3 billion dollar under the Sustainable Bond Scheme. This is a series of three currency issues covering different maturities of RMB, dollar, and euro bonds. This tranche of bonds attracted participation from various investor categories, with a strong subscription response, recording subscription amounts equivalent to over 15 billion dollar. The RMB green bonds with maturities of 20 and 30 years were the first issuance by the government, are the longest RMB bonds issued by the government to date, provide a new benchmark for the market, and further demonstrate the role of the Sustainable Bond Scheme. These bonds further enrich the selection of offshore RMB investment products in Hong Kong. Furthermore, global investors have reacted enthusiastically to the green bonds issued by the government, reflecting investors' affirmation of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers in the region to utilize Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable development funds, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Support Scheme," launched in May 2021, to provide support to eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. This program is widely welcomed by the industry; as of the end of 2024, the program has provided financing for approximately 500 issuances of green and sustainable debt instruments in Hong Kong, totaling over 140 billion dollar. The plan is extended for three years to 2027 in May 2024, and the funding scope is expanded to include convertible bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the plan is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries within the region to gradually reduce carbon by utilizing Hong Kong's transition financing platform. To provide financing for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, totaling over \$140 billion dollar (as of the end of 2024)—extending the period to 2027 and expanding the scope of financing to include transition financing instruments—the Hong Kong Monetary Authority actively promoted Hong Kong's sustainable finance platform, achieving favorable results in this endeavor. The Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued its fourth offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong in August, with a total value of 7 billion RMB, including 2.7 billion RMB in RMB green bonds, 1 billion RMB in sustainable bonds, and 900 million RMB in social responsibility bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People's Government issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, with a total value of 5 billion RMB, including 1.5 billion RMB in RMB green bonds. In October, the Hainan Provincial People's Government also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, with a total value of 3 billion RMB, including 1 billion RMB blue bonds and 1 billion RMB sustainable bonds. The aforementioned bond issuance activities repeatedly highlight Hong Kong's unique role in promoting the flow of green and sustainable financing between Mainland China and global regions. By leveraging the aforementioned measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the preferred platform for sustainable finance in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Markets Association, Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub for the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds in the region in 2024, with the total amount of related bonds arranged in Hong Kong reaching 43.1 billion dollar, accounting for 45% of the total in the region, and remains the largest hub in Asia. To catalyze sustainable finance innovation, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority assisted the government in issuing two series of landmark tokenized green bonds in 2023 and 2024, namely the first series of tokenized government green bonds globally, and the first series of multi-currency digital bonds globally. Regarding the issuance, the government provides support for the digitalization of assets and innovative technology in the green and sustainable finance sector for market participants in the region. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also launched the "Digital Bond Support Scheme" in November to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting the innovative development of the green and sustainable financial market in Hong Kong. The working groups for sustainable disclosure under the green and sustainable finance inter-agency steering group have consistently strived to adopt the "International Sustainability Disclosure Standards" (ISSB standards) in Hong Kong. The government issued the "Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap" in December 2024, providing a clear path for large public accountability entities to fully adopt ISSB standards no later than 2028. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always worked closely with local and international partners to provide support to entities at different stages of preparation to achieve high-quality sustainable disclosure, making sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive. It is worth mentioning that we continue to encourage the steering group's application of the "Private Company Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire" (questionnaire) launched in cooperation with CDP in 2022. This questionnaire provides user-friendly disclosure templates, facilitating the sustainable disclosure of enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The questionnaire was launched in February 2024 in electronic format, facilitating online submission for enterprises (see the QR code below). The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is optimizing the questionnaire to be more user-friendly based on industry feedback and the latest international developments, with specific measures including selecting core questions from the questionnaire and providing common use scenarios for the questionnaire. Furthermore, we also strive to improve the compatibility of the questionnaire and other supporting tools on the steering group website. For more information regarding the questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, in practice, in accordance with the latest global standards, should make high-quality sustainable disclosure in its "sustainable development report" to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains extensive content on operational risks related to climate from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, as well as plans and progress in implementing initiatives to achieve climate goals. For details regarding the sustainable disclosure of our own operations, please refer to the chapter "sustainable development" of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Given the volatility of the sustainable financial market, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is strengthening skills training in the banking sector and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulatory bodies and international stakeholders to fill knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local bank employees in sustainable finance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in collaboration with the Hong Kong Banking Association (Banking Association) launched the foundational level unit of "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" in July 2023 for banks. This module aims to assist professionals in the banking sector in acquiring knowledge and developing relevant professional capabilities in green and sustainable finance in a more effective manner, covering four main work areas: (1) Green and Sustainable Finance products and services; (2) Sustainable/climate risk management; (3) Sustainable disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainability strategy, compliance, and control. Furthermore, the professional-level "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit targeting mid-to-senior level bank employees responsible for related work was also launched in November. To provide necessary training to bank employees, the Banking Association, as the managing body for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit, launched the foundational level training course for this unit in May. Following the launch of the professional-level program in November, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will collaborate with the banking sector in 2025 to develop professional-level training courses. To address the further skills and training needs of the banking sector, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is currently collaborating with the banking sector on the "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030" study, with the objective of publishing the research findings in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the document "Future Banking Sector Talent 2021-2025" published in June 2020. The results of this research will provide important references for the industry, helping it formulate and adjust talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, in cooperation with the steering group, continues to assist in promoting the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme," subsidizing training in sustainable finance for employees, graduates, and students. As of December 2024, the program has 85 international and local courses registered as eligible training courses, and over 5,700 refund applications have been approved. The government announced in the "2025-2026 Fiscal Budget Proposal" that the plan will be extended until 2028. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through cooperation within the region and international cooperation. As a founding member of the "Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance" (CASI), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussion topics revolving around the global sustainable financial market, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority supports the establishment of a branch of the "Glasgow Net Zero Finance Alliance" (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage the GFANZ network and its expertise to enhance skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset holder and manager, the Monetary Authority actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Leveraging its experience in how financial performance and positive impact can mutually reinforce each other, the Monetary Authority adheres to a responsible investment philosophy when managing foreign exchange funds, prioritizes sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights over the assets. The Monetary Authority invests prudently according to the principle of "preserve principal first, long-term appreciation," believing that thorough consideration of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors helps reduce related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of the investment. As a firm signatory of the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the Monetary Authority is committed to advancing its responsible investment work. We place special emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of foreign exchange funds and pursue more optimal long-term risk-adjusted returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment tools to direct capital towards sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). The Monetary Authority contributes to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by leveraging its role as a major investor. In September, the Monetary Authority issued the "Monetary Authority ESG Expectations" and made the document public to investment partners through the annual ESG workshop and the Monetary Authority website. We, investors, regulatory bodies, and international organizations with similar philosophies, jointly develop industry operating standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment by the financial industry and central banks. Through these cooperative efforts, we are committed to promoting a future where finance and sustainability go hand in hand. The Monetary Authority announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan") in October, outlining how the "investment portfolio" of foreign exchange funds can achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and mobilize partner support for a low-carbon economic transition, further solidifying its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Foreign Exchange Funds Advisory Committee, chaired by the Director of the Ministry of Finance, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented in the investment management of the foreign exchange funds by the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. The primary guiding principles establish the tone for the Monetary Authority to practice responsible investment while also considering the investment objectives of the foreign exchange funds. The Investment Committee under the purview of the Foreign Exchange Funds Advisory Committee is chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority and is responsible for supervising the ESG and climate-related risks associated with foreign exchange funds investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policy, and monitors the implementation status through the regular meeting reports of the sustainable investment subcommittee of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office is chaired by the Chief Strategist and is responsible for coordinating and supervising all ESG work of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. The motions and progress of work discussed by the ESG Committee at the quarterly meeting will be reported to the President of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee, regularly convened, is chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority, the CEO of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, and the Chief Strategist, to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures of the Monetary Authority's various functions, including the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, in order to implement the Monetary Authority's overall ESG objectives. The sustainable investment subcommittee and the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office collaborate closely in integrating ESG factors, and assist senior personnel of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office in managing the ESG risks and opportunities, especially climate-related ones, for various investment projects: - Public Market Investments - The situation after credit, regulatory, and supervisory committees composed of senior personnel from the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office have reviewed the ESG factors integrated into credit risk models based on the opinions of the sustainable investment subcommittee, and the ESG status of fixed-income asset portfolios is monitored through regular reports from the risk management and supervision departments. Furthermore, the sustainable investment subcommittee also participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring process of external investment managers for stock portfolios from an ESG perspective (see Section "Promoting Active Exercise of Ownership" in the "Risk Management" section on page 39 for details). Private Market Investment - The Investment Committee, chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority, will consider the ESG-related assess made by the private market investment and risk management teams on each investment recommendation. The Monetary Authority understands the physical and transition risks and related opportunities brought by climate change, which will affect the long-term financial performance of foreign exchange funds investment projects. The United Nations Environment Programme's "2024 Emissions Gap Report" predicts that unless global large-scale mobilization rapidly reduces greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Policy changes due to rising temperatures, technological development, and behavioral shifts may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the frequency and severity of extreme weather events are increasing, also bringing additional physical damage and financial loss risks to investment projects. In the face of these challenges, governments and industries worldwide are shifting towards sustainable solutions, creating investment opportunities with potentially long-term prospects in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies, and sustainable infrastructure. The Monetary Authority believes that its investment objectives align with the investment goals of foreign exchange funds, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG factors. The Monetary Authority has set a goal for the foreign exchange funds' investment portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and will continue to advance this objective through an orderly, multi-pronged approach (see Figure 3). The Monetary Authority announced the "Action Plan" in 2024, which solidified commitments and efforts related to the foreign exchange funds and climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the low-carbon economic transition, the Monetary Authority tends to proactively engage in communication rather than excluding or withdrawing investment from investment projects. Investing in sustainable future foreign exchange funds' investment portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier—actively expanding the scope and types of sustainable investments, particularly in the public and private markets with a focus on climate transition—integrating ESG factors into each investment decision, with particular consideration for the prospects of climate change and transition—establishing clear ESG expectations that comply with international standards and best practices, and requiring all external investment managers, investment companies, and trading counterparties to adhere to them—committing to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the foreign exchange fund's equity portfolio by 67% from the 2017 level by 2030 or earlier through investment support for regional transition—continuing to communicate with external investment managers to optimize investment opportunities to drive the transition—continuing to discover and prioritize high-quality investment opportunities that promote Asian transition and bring positive impacts to the global stage. First, maintaining a diversified and stable asset portfolio plays a key role in achieving the primary investment objective of the foreign exchange funds. Directly excluding certain categories or industries will narrow the investable universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risk. Through compatible approaches, the Monetary Authority can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transformation, possessing excellent technology and good corporate governance to respond to changing global climate trends, including companies belonging to high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires a core "brown" industries transformation. Only exclude relevant investment projects or divestment without helping solve carbon emission problems. Conversely, the Monetary Authority supports these industries' transformation towards sustainable and low-carbon operating methods by investing strategic capital and actively exercising ownership rights, thereby bringing about beneficial changes for themselves and for the global. The net-zero investment policy has evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with reliable transition prospects to drive comprehensive decarbonization of the overall economy. As owners of global assets, the Monetary Authority understands the long-term resilience of asset portfolios, which not only depends on the adjustment of the asset portfolio itself but also on broad economic transformation. Although there is no perfect single solution, the Monetary Authority improved its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive the transition, while supporting foreign exchange funds and global net-zero goals. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors into fundamental analysis and guiding the decarbonization tilt of asset portfolios, as well as thematic investing in various asset classes that align with the path toward net-zero emissions. In the public markets, this may involve a tilt in asset portfolios towards ESG-leading or climate solution-providing companies, in conjunction with supervision and promotion of corporate transformation of assets. In the private market, there may place greater emphasis on promoting transformative investment projects. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the Monetary Authority continues to seek investment opportunities that can promote the climate transition and simultaneously enhance the long-term resilience of foreign exchange funds asset portfolios. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the foreign exchange funds' investment portfolio, with financial performance aligning with that of the relevant asset portfolios (Figure 5). Public Market Investments - the Monetary Authority has launched an active global equity investment portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and has extended the application of a customized low-carbon stock index to the other two asset portfolios managed by external investment managers. The Monetary Authority continues to seek to provide green, social responsibility, and sustainability (GSS) bonds that offer competitive returns while providing funding for sustainable projects (see the related case study in the "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds" section). Private Market Investment - The Monetary Authority is committed to building resilient long-term growth portfolios and seizing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. The Monetary Authority is again leveraging its extensive network and expertise to actively seek and review investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including establishing strategic partnership collaborations with multinational organizations (see the section "Cooperation in Addressing Climate Challenges from Asia to the Global"). Passive investment portfolios using ESG indices as investment benchmarks - customized decarbonization strategies for passive and active quantitative investment portfolios not using ESG indices - active investment portfolios with governance as the theme - active ESG investment portfolios with a theme of sustainability and climate transition - projects with sustainability characteristics, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and buildings and warehouses with green certifications - funds with a theme of energy transition and decarbonization in the global, Asian, and global south - green, social responsibility, and sustainability bonds - a green bond fund managed by an international organization - the "Joint Loan Portfolio Management Programme" (MCPP) managed by an international financial institution, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets - the "MCPP One Planet" project, providing climate-related investments in emerging markets compliant with the Paris Agreement. The Monetary Authority invests in green bonds issued by a semi-official institution. The funds raised by the green bonds are allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading the old equipment of several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrade projects cover the optimization of monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits in wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to continuous wastewater and sludge treatment, these facilities will process the dewatered sludge through composting or reuse to produce fertilizers, charcoal, cement, and other building materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilize the gas generated during the sludge treatment process to provide energy for the boiler and generate electricity. The Monetary Authority invested in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. These bonds provide funding for multiple projects, including the repair of a national canal system. As one of the largest irrigation systems in the country, the canal is designed to divert excess water from the river to arid regions. The main objective of this project is to repair the increasingly deteriorated lining of the canal to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency, and reclaim water-inundated areas. Furthermore, the project also provides skills training to local stakeholders, promoting the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies such as micro-irrigation and sustainable farming methods.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to being a responsible and sustainable institution. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, in 2024, made one of its key priorities in fulfilling this commitment to plan to advance the target date for achieving net-zero emissions for the institution's operations to 2030, twenty years earlier than the original target, consistent with the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan." In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also commits to fostering employee training and mental and physical well-being, striving to promote financial inclusion, and enhancing the financial knowledge of the public. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee) is chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and is the principal decision-making body for various organizational sustainability measures. To demonstrate the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's commitment to climate change, the Steering Committee approved the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's new target to achieve net-zero emissions in its operations by 2030 or earlier, in October 2024, as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"). At the departmental level, the Assistant President (Institutional Development and Operations) provides guidance on sustainable development measures concerning institutional operations, employee physical and mental well-being, and social engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The administrative group serves as the coordinator and central hub for the implementation, communication, and reporting of sustainable development measures. A special team of green office staff and volunteer service groups, composed of employees from different operating departments, is responsible for providing another layer of support. The former is a platform for brainstorming suggestions on how to create a green working environment, and the latter aims to cultivate a culture of employee participation in volunteer activities. To commend The Hong Kong Monetary Authority for its commitment to the environment, employees, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Social Services Association has continuously awarded the "15 Years + United in Care" emblem to the Monetary Authority from 2006 to in 2024, a period of 18 years. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainable development strategy continues to adopt a structure composed of three pillars: environment, employee, and social responsibility. Focusing on carbon reduction and digitalization in the daily operations of The Monetary Authority, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 or earlier—adopting green procurement requirements based on government guidance—promoting more environmentally friendly operational solutions within the financial industry and the broader society—building a proactive team and talent pool to achieve The Monetary Authority's strategic objectives—fostering a work environment that promotes collaboration and inclusion, emphasizing diversity and strengthening employee belonging—providing a high-quality working environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle—cultivating a culture of social concern—incorporating social considerations into procurement procedures and supply chain management—promoting financial inclusion, and enhancing public financial literacy through consumer education activities. The Monetary Authority is concerned about climate change and sets an example. In October 2024, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced plans to advance the target date for its institution's operations to achieve net-zero emissions to 2030, twenty years earlier than the original commitment, as part of an Action Plan. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has revised the roadmap towards net-zero transformation, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of daily operations, concentrating on reducing carbon emissions, energy saving, and paper reduction, as well as waste recycling and reuse, while fully utilizing the improvements in the local power company's generation fuel mix. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has established a digitalized work environment to improve efficiency while simultaneously reducing the carbon footprint. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority understands the importance of cultivating a sustainable development culture, and therefore, through the continuous organization of promotional programs and activities, encourages employees to actively adopt practices that contribute to sustainable development. Under the primary net-zero emissions goal for 2030, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has been exploring the adoption of carbon embedded tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and to pursue low-carbon procurement as much as possible. In this regard, since 2023, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has comprehensively offset the carbon emissions from air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset programs. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will expand carbon embedding and carbon offset programs to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the environmental commitments related to actual operations mentioned above, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to promote the market's low-carbon transition by introducing procedures for electronic document submission and processing, as well as promoting electronic payments and the collection of coins back into circulation. The remainder of this chapter details the strategies of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority in leading environmental protection, and promoting the physical and mental well-being of employee and care for society. Under the overall institutional risk management framework of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the risk committee, chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, is responsible for supervising and reviewing the potential risks and threats that The Monetary Authority faces in its daily operations, including those caused by climate change. To more effectively assess the impact of climate change on operations, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has identified different climate-related risks and reviewed the actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring continued operation, the office of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has designed integrated measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority regularly updates contingency plans and comprehensive measures, which include not only the offices but also communication and computer facilities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility drills to ensure employees are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has consistently monitored the transition risks it faces by tracking greenhouse gas emissions generated by its operations, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's latest climate goal is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 emissions related to institutional operations by 2030 or earlier. These targets were formulated using the methodology of the "Science-Based Targets Initiative." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority adopts the Greenhouse Gas Accounting System to measure and report emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from gasoline vehicles. Given the nature of the operations, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's main greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions caused by the consumption of fossil fuels to generate electricity. Due to the absence of data from individual suppliers, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has adopted a conservative approach to estimate the Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital products) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste transported to landfills and employee air travel and commuting. The detailed calculation results for 2023 and in 2024 are contained in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria for verification are stated in the "Verification Statement" attached at the end of this report. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority actively implements and adheres to the same climate-related standards that the banks it supervises and the financial system it inspects comply with. As a first step towards green mobility, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority began replacing its gasoline vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024, and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve comprehensive green mobility. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to integrate environmental factors into the design, operations, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in the renovation projects in 2024, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority reused existing furniture and finishing materials or purchased new items at a discounted price through trade-ins, reducing waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority regularly reviews the energy consumption and energy saving measures of the office and data center, and in 2024 upgraded the data center facility project to adopt a modular design uninterruptible power supply system, further optimizing the energy usage efficiency (Power Usage Effectiveness, abbreviated as PUE) of the data center, which has obtained the "Green Building Environmental Assessment" certification. This design can flexibly expand capacity, improve operational efficiency during partial loads, and be equipped with advanced refrigeration technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has enhanced internal virtual collaboration through digital work and streamlined workflows to effectively reduce paper reduction. Furthermore, in accordance with the software update cycle of manufacturers, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority can extend the usage period of liquid and desktop devices, thereby extending the safe usage period of the devices. To reduce waste generated by the office, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority adheres to the "4R" principles, which are refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle, and regularly conducts waste audits to assist in formulating targeted waste management strategies. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has placed recycling bins in convenient locations in the office to collect different materials. To improve recycling rates, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority established beverage box and plastic fruit net bag recycling bins in 2024. Furthermore, starting from November 2022, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will send the kitchen waste collected to a recycling center in Hong Kong. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority participated in the Environmental Protection Administration's "activities waste reduction commitment" in May in 2024, committing to take measures to reduce the waste generated by various activities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to prioritize the procurement of goods that meet the environmental standards of the government's "Green Procurement List," especially electronic goods and office consumables. To reduce aviation travel carbon emissions, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority encourages employees to carefully plan their itineraries, for example, by combining multiple trips when participating in overseas activities. At the institutional level, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing annual aviation travel carbon emissions by approximately 10%. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority participates in the "Gold Standard" carbon offset programs to offset its remaining aviation travel carbon emissions. This plan focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority arranged multiple learning activities for employees, such as lectures and tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance employees' understanding of environmental sustainability issues. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority held its first "Monetary Authority Green Month" from April 22, in 2024, until the end of May in 2024, with the theme "Green Thinking, Green Living, Green Work." This is a good opportunity to demonstrate the commitment and motivation of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority in promoting environmental sustainability in internal operations. The content of the entire activities includes the "Sustainable Development BINGO score card" to encourage employees to practice Green Living, a "Save the Earth" quiz game, and a workshop on caring for indoor plants, "Kokedama," originating from Japan. Additionally, we share the results of the waste audits, and the operator of the community recycling center will introduce the best practices for recycling operations. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month," The Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched a recycling activities for approximately six months in October, highlighting the responsible disposal of waste and reminding employees that changing even small individual habits can significantly improve the organization's overall recycling performance. One highlight of the activities was the launch of the "Green 'Adapt' Action" short film, featuring insights from several senior executives on recycling tips. The activities also launched a series of screen saver programs, design-prominent posters, online articles, and electronic prompts to remind employees to practice waste reduction and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority conducted an employee survey to understand their awareness of sustainable development and to collect their opinions on proposed measures for the green office.
