The investigation results will assist in formulating future sustainable development training activities and waste management strategies. As the central bank institution of Hong Kong, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority views itself as an important member in facilitating transformation, and is therefore committed to leading and accelerating the low-carbon transition, promoting sustainable development practices in the financial industry and society as a whole. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has introduced multiple measures to enhance the efficiency of external procedures. Following the successful launch of the "Shared Data Submission Platform" in 2023, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will expand the platform's service scope in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as value-added payment tool operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data for the operations of banks. The purpose of expanding the scope of platform services is to further simplify the submission process for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and simultaneously consolidate The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's commitment to sustainable development. Other new measures launched in 2024 include allowing banks to respond to The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's survey questionnaires with the SurveyTool to simplify the submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system, providing users with a central platform for advanced search and bank-related document functions.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency independently verifies the environmental data of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The data includes the total energy consumption for 2024, greenhouse gas emissions for scope 1 and scope 2, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel, as well as their respective densities. Furthermore, the data also includes the scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from the activities related to purchased goods and services, capital products, fuel and energy, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste) and employee commuting generated in 2023 and 2024, and their corresponding emission factors. The greenhouse gas emissions data of the HKMA are compiled according to the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (referred to as "GHG Protocol"), which is prepared by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council of Sustainable Development's greenhouse gas emissions system. The scope of verification covers 6 office and warehouse assets, of which 5 offices are located in 1) International Finance Centre Phase II, 2) Harmony Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 5) Global Trade Centre, with the warehouse in 6) Lcs Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance of the accuracy and reliability of the data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and support evidence from six selected assets. This verification work is conducted in accordance with the "International Verification Engagement Guidelines 3000 (Revised Edition)" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provision for "Verification engagements other than the audit or review of historical financial data." The verification procedure is designed to make opinions and summaries to obtain a reasonable degree of assurance. The verification process is determined according to the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The validation process involved tracing the selected sample data back to its source to test the integrity and accuracy of the data, and also reviewed the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducted reliability testing. The validation process also includes verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, visiting representatives responsible for preparing the data, and selecting representative data and information for verification. The relevant original data and supporting evidence have also undergone detailed review during the validation process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of information. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency's verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reasonably guarantees the data and summarizes: - The data is substantively accurate and reliable. The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is sufficient. Shen Xiaoyin Review Supervisor The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
